# A calm place to write for your Astro site.

Zeku is a native app that opens your Astro project directly, with live-preview markdown, frontmatter that knows your schema, and a publish button.

![The Zeku window: a file tree on the left, a markdown post in live preview in the middle, with its frontmatter above the text](https://zeku.dev/_astro/hero-editor-dark@2x.DLPXFem6_Z8FlqA.webp)![The Zeku window: a file tree on the left, a markdown post in live preview in the middle, with its frontmatter above the text](https://zeku.dev/_astro/hero-editor-light@2x.B9i6oWP-_1BwiLU.webp)

Reads the `content.config.ts` you already have.Edits files in place.Pushes to your repo.

## The one-minute film

[![](https://zeku.dev/_astro/zeku-film-poster.B7QEaUXE_Z11zhEY.jpg)Play the film](https://youtu.be/yk1nQJC_mpg)

Your project

### Opens your repo and reads its schema.

Point Zeku at an Astro project and it finds the content folder on its own. Every collection your `content.config.ts` declares shows up, nested ones included, with field types from the schemas `astro sync` writes.

Nothing is copied into a second config. It is read fresh every time you open the project, so it can never go stale.

- Collections from your config, in the order you think in
- A file tree with Content and Site views
- Any folder of markdown opens too

![The Zeku dashboard showing a Posts collection as cards, with tabs for Pages, Projects, Docs, and Special collections read from the project's config](https://zeku.dev/_astro/dashboard-cards-dark@2x.CakKPEsO_Q4OFB.webp)![The Zeku dashboard showing a Posts collection as cards, with tabs for Pages, Projects, Docs, and Special collections read from the project's config](https://zeku.dev/_astro/dashboard-cards-light@2x.Bo7MQEux_ZE6J3f.webp)

Frontmatter

### Frontmatter that knows your schema.

Zeku draws a form from your collection schema. Enum fields offer their allowed values, `reference()` fields look up entries in the target collection, dates get a picker, booleans get a checkbox, and required fields are marked.

Keys your schema does not know keep working, and dates are written back in the format you choose.

src/content/posts/field-notes.md

```
---
title: Field notes from a slow week
description: What I learned writing every
  morning for a month.
date: 2026-09-18
author: david
category: essays
tags:
  - writing
  - habits
draft: false
---
```

Frontmatter

title \*Field notes from a slow week

descriptionWhat I learned writing every morning for a month.

dateSep 18, 2026

authorDavid V. Kimball authors

categoryessays guidesessaysnotes

tagswritinghabits

draft

Writing

### Markdown that renders while you write.

Syntax fades until your cursor reaches it. Callouts, Starlight admonitions, tables, footnotes, math, mermaid diagrams, and Expressive Code blocks render in place.

YouTube, Bluesky, CodePen, and Gist embeds show up inline, and raw HTML renders where it sits. Flip to source any time.

![A post in Zeku's live preview with a rendered callout, a table, and a code block with a title](https://zeku.dev/_astro/live-preview-dark@2x._vqlY-ii_Z2cDni3.webp)![A post in Zeku's live preview with a rendered callout, a table, and a code block with a title](https://zeku.dev/_astro/live-preview-light@2x.BP86anvF_Z1WUmro.webp)

Preview

### See the real site as you write.

Zeku starts your project's own `astro dev`, with whichever of pnpm, npm, yarn, or bun it uses, and shows the page beside the editor.

It renders with your own components, layout, and CSS, so what you see is what ships.

![Zeku with the editor on the left and the live Astro dev server preview of the same page on the right](https://zeku.dev/_astro/site-preview-dark@2x.DOn_TEyg_Z2qkKqP.webp)![Zeku with the editor on the left and the live Astro dev server preview of the same page on the right](https://zeku.dev/_astro/site-preview-light@2x.w4asX9QO_Z1ho5IT.webp)

Publish

### Publish without a terminal.

See what changed, write a commit message, and push. Zeku pulls first so you never clobber work from another machine.

Your host builds the push the way it always has. Zeku never deploys anything itself.

![The Zeku publish dialog listing changed files above a commit message field and a Publish button](https://zeku.dev/_astro/publish-dark@2x.Yj7tx7QU_Z1FdmsE.webp)![The Zeku publish dialog listing changed files above a commit message field and a Publish button](https://zeku.dev/_astro/publish-light@2x.DVXMqY0h_106Hl6.webp)

![The Zeku SEO panel scoring a post on title, description, keyword placement, headings, and alt text](https://zeku.dev/_astro/seo-audit-dark@2x.Dla9wo2b_1bedUz.webp)![The Zeku SEO panel scoring a post on title, description, keyword placement, headings, and alt text](https://zeku.dev/_astro/seo-audit-light@2x.DnudOGvR_Z25HxDj.webp)

SEO

### An audit for every page, and every collection.

Title and description length, keyword placement, heading order, alt text, reading level, and internal links that resolve. Run it on one page with `Ctrl`  `Shift`  `A`, or score a whole collection at once. You set the thresholds.

![A Starlight docs project in Zeku, with pages listed in the same order as the site's sidebar](https://zeku.dev/_astro/starlight-sidebar-dark@2x.Bqq6vAE1_2kt4jD.webp)![A Starlight docs project in Zeku, with pages listed in the same order as the site's sidebar](https://zeku.dev/_astro/starlight-sidebar-light@2x.D61IqwZa_JOAGa.webp)

Starlight

### Docs sites sort like their sidebar.

Starlight projects list pages in the order your sidebar shows them, so the dashboard matches what your readers see.

- ### MDX component builder


Press Ctrl+/ to search your own components, fill in props, pick a hydration directive, and insert. The import is added for you.

- ### Images land in the right place


Drag, drop, or paste and the file is copied into your assets folder with a clean name and a relative link. Stock photo search is built in.

- ### A dashboard per collection


Cards or list, search, tag and draft filters, and bulk actions for publishing, tagging, or setting a frontmatter key on many entries at once.

- ### Theme settings as a form


Themes that mark their options in src/config.ts, like Axis and Astro Modular, get a real settings screen. Everything else opens as source.

- ### Spellcheck that stays local


A bundled English dictionary plus your own word list. It skips code and URLs, and nothing you write leaves your machine to be checked.

- ### Hard to lose work


Autosave, crash recovery kept outside your repo, and a prompt instead of an overwrite when a file changes on disk under you.

- ### Zen mode



[... middle omitted — see footer ...]


If your site uses Astro content collections, yes. Zeku is tested on the 200 most popular Astro themes and the official starters: see [how each one did](https://zeku.dev/themes). Themes that mark their settings in `src/config.ts`, like Axis and Astro Modular, also get a real settings form, and Starlight docs sites sort the way their sidebar does.

Do I have to stop using Obsidian or Vault CMS?

No. Zeku never reads or writes `.obsidian`, so both can point at the same folder and neither rewrites the other. Vault CMS stays free.

How does publishing work?

Zeku uses your own git. It shows what changed, commits with your message, pulls, and pushes. Your host deploys the push the way it always does. Zeku never deploys anything itself.

Is there any AI in it?

No, on purpose. Use whatever AI tools you like for building the site. Zeku is where you write.

Is it on Mac or Linux?

Yes, both in beta. On a Mac, Zeku runs on macOS 10.15 Catalina and later, on Apple Silicon and Intel: run `curl -fsSL https://zeku.dev/install.sh | bash` in Terminal, or download the .dmg from the [download page](https://zeku.dev/download#mac). On Linux, Zeku runs on x86\_64 with glibc 2.35 or later, such as Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora 36 or current Arch: run the same command in a terminal to install it for your account, or download the AppImage, .deb, or .rpm from the [download page](https://zeku.dev/download#linux). The command and the AppImage update themselves; the .deb and .rpm update when you install a newer one. One license covers Zeku on any platform, on up to 3 computers.

Is it a subscription?

No. You pay once, and every update after that is free. After the 14-day trial, Zeku keeps working and reminds you to buy.

## Open your project. Start writing.

Try it free. No account or setup, and nothing added to your repo.

### An app your team will actually enjoy using

A clean, responsive interface that gets out of the way so people can focus on writing.

- Intuitive UI with dark mode, keyboard shortcuts and drag-and-drop uploads
- Instant full-text search across every collection and asset
- Full-fledged asset library with folders, filters and previews
- Spreadsheet-style editing of many entries at once
- Works on phones and tablets, with quick QR code sign-in
- Drafts are backed up automatically, and you’re warned before overwriting someone else’s changes
- Accessible by design, with full keyboard and screen reader support

[See features for editors →](https://sveltiacms.app/en/features/editors)

![A list of blog posts with thumbnails, publish dates, authors and tags](https://sveltiacms.app/images/landing/entry-list-dark.webp?20261015)![A list of blog posts with thumbnails, publish dates, authors and tags](https://sveltiacms.app/images/landing/entry-list-light.webp?20261015)

### One config file, no servers to maintain

Describe your content in a single config file and add a script tag. No backend to host, no database to back up, no upgrades to install.

- Works with Astro, Eleventy, Hugo, Jekyll, Next.js, SvelteKit and any other framework
- GitHub, GitLab, Gitea and Forgejo backends, with OAuth or token sign-in
- Edit a local repository directly in the browser, without a proxy server
- JSON schema validation and autocompletion for your config file
- JavaScript API for custom field types, previews and editor components
- npm package with TypeScript types that loads nothing from third-party CDNs
- Official Agent Skill and llms.txt for AI coding assistants

[See features for developers →](https://sveltiacms.app/en/features/developers)

admin/config.yml

```
backend:
  name: github
  repo: user/repo

media_folder: /public/media

collections:
  - name: posts
    label: Posts
    folder: /content/posts
    fields:
      - { name: title, widget: string }
      - { name: date, widget: datetime }
      - { name: body, widget: richtext }
```

### A website your whole team can keep up to date

Give staff and volunteers an easy way to update your site, with no license fees, no servers to run and an optional review step before changes go live.

- Free and open source forever, with no per-seat or per-site pricing
- Host for free on Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel, etc.
- Multilingual sites with one-click AI translation
- Editorial Workflow for reviewing changes before they go live
- Optional built-in image optimizer converts uploads to WebP
- Trusted by government agencies, universities and nonprofits worldwide

[Browse the showcase →](https://sveltiacms.app/en/showcase)

Build with the frameworks you already use, then give clients a friendly CMS that needs little training.

Stageshow is a skill that helps your agent make better faux UI.[1](https://benji.org/stageshow#user-content-fn-1) Most good models can do this now without a dedicated skill, but the results often look sloppy and heavy-handed, and that's the gap Stageshow is for.

Made with Stageshow.

I've made a lot of these by hand, and they take far longer than they should. No single part is especially hard, but there are a hundred small decisions and every one of them shows. Stageshow is my attempt to write those decisions down, so an agent can make them too.

* * *

# Getting started

```
npx skills add benjitaylor/skills --skill stageshow
```

That adds the skill for any agent: Grok Build, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, etc. Then ask for something small: one interaction, in one product, at one size.

```
A small looping demo for our homepage hero: someone assigns an issue to a teammate.
```

The agent reads the skill, starts from the closest example, builds the demo, then films it and fixes what it finds. What you get is an ordinary React component, so you can put it anywhere and change it like the rest of your code.

It still may not nail it in one shot. The first pass is usually a big step up from what an agent makes on its own, but most demos still take me a few rounds of feedback.

fair warning

* * *

# What's in it

references/rehearse.md

references/bento.md

references/framing.md

references/craft.md

SKILL.mdThe one idea

It reads as a real product, simplified to what the viewer needs, framed with intent, and every motion has a cause.

Stagekit/

Acme CorpPublish

What the agent works with.

`SKILL.md`

What the agent reads first: the one idea, the five ways faux UI fails, a seven-step workflow, a table of the gold examples, the kit at a glance and a summary of framing.

`references/`

Craft (restraint, type, spacing, colour), motion (story, pace, the cursor), framing (crops, satellites, layouts), grids, looks and backgrounds, annotations, real products and brand marks, filming and the checklist, good and bad pairs side by side, and every kit part's props. Most rules came from reviewing real attempts, and each gives its reason.

`examples/`

Dozens of gold examples the agent starts from and holds its work against, from a hero demo and bento grids to a phone swipe and a dashboard paired with a lock screen.

`kit/`

A small set of React parts the agent can build with, plain code that lives with your demo. It makes the hard parts hold up; it doesn't supply a look. The stage, windows and phones drawn from real geometry, motion that has to survive frame by frame, and a few quiet parts to restyle.

`scripts/`

film.mjs films a demo, lays the frames on a contact sheet and reports what it can measure. jumps.mjs catches one-frame snaps a sheet misses, and layout.mjs checks that text and controls fit their boxes.

* * *

# The playground

The skill also comes with a playground. Run it from the skill's folder:

```
npm install
npm run dev
```

It has every example in the skill, the kit's parts on their own, and a set of comparisons: the same thing done badly and done well, side by side. They're there for the agent as much as for you. "Don't shrink the whole app into a card" is easy to agree with and easy to skip, but much harder to ignore once you see both side by side.

* * *

# What the skill teaches

The skill is built around one sentence:

It reads as a real product, simplified to what the viewer needs, framed with intent, and every motion has a cause.

the whole skill, really

Faux UI from agents tends to go wrong in the same few ways. The most common are _too much_ (real words in every cell, packed tight), _too little_ (a wireframe that doesn't read as a product) and _boxed_ (the whole window shrunk into a card, like a pasted screenshot). Then there's _flat_, where everything has the same weight, and _bland_, where the brief's style never shows up.

Here's one demo going from the first to the last, the way the agent builds it: someone assigns a support conversation to Maya.

The whole screen in quiet greys, real words only where the story is. Correct, but boxed in like a screenshot.The window pins to the corner and runs off the edge, and the one card the story needs slides in over it.Now it plays: the menu opens, Maya is picked, it all resets. With no cursor, it seems to run by itself.A cursor gives each change a cause, except the last, where Maya vanishes with nothing there to undo her.The avatar flies to its row and holds, then the cursor undoes it on screen, so the loop has no visible seam.

Left to itself, an agent drifts toward the first. It knows what a support inbox contains, so it fills every row. The skill has it keep only the words the story needs and use placeholder lines for the rest, so the inbox still looks full without asking you to read it. It also decides the crop first, so it doesn't waste time building things nobody will see.

* * *

# How a demo is built

Every demo is a stage: a canvas with a design size. Its contents are drawn from state, and a script changes that state one beat at a time. The cursor is part of the stage, and it aims at things by name.

The code below, drawn out: the stage crops the window, the cursor aims at a name, the state flips, and each beat lights as it runs.

```
async function script(a: Act<S>) {
  await a.click({ at: "share" }); // arcs there, presses
  await a.set({ open: true }); // resolves once painted
  await a.wait(2000); // the payoff holds
  await a.click({ at: "close" });
  await a.set({ open: false });
  await a.move({ x: 600, y: 300 }); // back where it began
}
```

Parts stay mounted while they transition, so they can move in and out instead of popping. Positions are measured, so the cursor lands in the right place and overlays line up at any size. And the kit handles the motion that's hard to get right by hand, like a number that rolls only the digits that changed, a card flying into a slot, or a message forming out of the text field.

There's also a camera, so a stage can push in on the important bit and pull back out. It sits on top of the scene, so you don't have to change the scene to use it.

* * *

# Limitations

The checks catch mistakes, not dull ideas. A demo can pass every one and still not be worth watching, so you still have to look at it yourself.

It also can't draw, so anything that needs illustration or photography is better made by hand and dropped in.

Most of the rules started as a note on a real demo, like "the shadow is too harsh" or "this title isn't centred." Once a note is in the skill, every demo after it gets it for free. You can do the same: when you correct a demo, ask the agent to add the note to the skill.

* * *

# For now

Model taste is getting better with every release, and I suspect a skill like this is only useful for a while, since much of what it teaches and includes could soon come built in.

Some of it already has. Early on in making this, the references had rules a newer model simply didn't need, like keeping the traffic lights the right size, and as the models improved those rules quietly stopped doing anything.

Others have held up across every model I've tried, mostly the ones about framing and motion. Models are perfectly capable of getting those right, but they don't seem to know that they matter until something tells them.

Until then, it helps, and every demo made with it is a small, well-built example of this kind of UI, which is the sort of thing models learn from. If it plays a small part in making itself unnecessary, that's fine by me.

If you want to give it a go:

```
npx skills add benjitaylor/skills --skill stageshow
```

## Footnotes

1. The products shown in the demos, along with their names, logos and interfaces, belong to their owners. The demos are illustrations made for this post and aren't affiliated with or endorsed by them. [↩](https://benji.org/stageshow#user-content-fnref-1)

2. Taste sounds mysterious, but most of it is small decisions made over and over until you know which ones hold up. That's why it can be written down. It also means Stageshow is my taste, not a neutral one. [↩](https://benji.org/stageshow#user-content-fnref-2)

[New sitereal 1.0.2 is out](https://sitereal.app/changelog) # A visual builder for Astro that writes real files. [Start trial](https://account.sitereal.app/start?plan=trial) [Read the docs](https://sitereal.app/docs) Presentation of the sitereal app and its functionalities. The builder ## Draw the page on a canvas that edits files. Every breakpoint at once, a tree carrying your own class names, and a Style panel writing into the one rule that actually styles the element. Select a heading and .hero\_\_title opens — not a copy of it. [Explore the builder](https://sitereal.app/builder) Features ## Everything your site needs, built into sitereal. ### Design Compose responsive pages on a visual canvas. ### Code Edit the real files, here or in your editor. ### Agents Let Claude Code build and maintain pages. ### MCP Connect any MCP client to the open project. ### Reuse Components, templates, snippets and presets. ### Design system Eighteen modules of tokens you can switch off. ### Content One schema gives you types, forms and queries. ### Motion Reveals and scroll links, as plain attributes. ### SEO Titles, structured data, sitemap and robots. ### Ship Its own git repository. Hosts anywhere. Real code ## Paste HTML, get a tree. Read the tree, get the HTML back. Same class names, no builder-owned wrapper, and no generated name you did not choose. LayerOutput 1 2 3Pricing 4 5 6Yearly 7€69

8 9 10 11 Format HTML ⇄ LayerOutput Search… sectionPricing divContainer h2Title divGrid articleCard h3Name pPrice Workflow ## Three moves, and the third one is git push. There is no publish button that phones home, because there is nothing to phone — branches, pull and push are plain git against your own remote. 1. Step 01 ### Open a folder Point sitereal at an Astro project you already have, or scaffold a new one. It gets its own git repository at once — a site’s history has nothing to do with the tool that drew it. 2. Step 02 ### Compose Sections, containers, elements. Style through the token layer or write the CSS yourself in the same panel: the two are views of one stylesheet, not a round trip. 3. Step 03 ### Commit Save, and real files land under src/. Push them. Deploy to Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare, a bucket or your own box. Nothing on that server has ever heard of sitereal. main Branches main pricing-page docs/rewrite new-branch-name Origin origin/main · 2 commits behind Pull from GitHub Commit Pricing page, second pass Commit all changes (7) GitHub meinaufwind/sitereal · 3 to push Commit & push to origin/main ### Branches Every branch the repository has, local and on origin, and a field that starts a new one. Switching keeps unfinished work with the branch it belongs to and hands it back when you return, instead of dragging it onto another one. ### Pull Fetch and rebase onto origin, autostashed, so whatever you were in the middle of survives it. On a conflict git stops and you are handed its own message, not a summary of it. ### Push Stage, commit and push to origin, in one press. Nothing is ever committed or pushed on your behalf — the engine runs git when you ask it to and at no other moment. Hosting ## A folder of finished pages. Nothing to attack, nothing to wait for. sitereal builds an Astro site, so what you upload is HTML, CSS and images. No PHP on the host, no admin login on the public site, no plugin surface and no database unless you asked for one — and because every page was rendered before anyone asked for it, there is nothing left to compute while a visitor waits. ### Nothing on the host to break into A static site is files being served. There is no wp-admin, no plugin with a CVE in it, no database credentials sitting on the machine. The builder runs on your own computer and is never part of the deployed site, so the attack surface a CMS gives away for free simply is not there — and a form's delivery keys stay in environment variables on your host, never in the page. ### Zero JavaScript until you ask for some Astro renders your components at build time and ships no framework runtime by default. Interactivity is an island, loaded only where you place one, and sitereal's own runtimes — motion, navigation, forms, overlays — are a few kilobytes each and emitted only for the pages that actually use them. ### The page is finished before the request arrives Every route is built once and served as a file, from a CDN, an object store or the cPanel plan a client already pays for. Nothing renders per visit, so there is no cache plugin to invalidate, no page that gets slower under load, and hosting costs what static hosting costs. Publish ## One button puts it online. From your computer to your host. Publish builds the site on your machine and uploads it to Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare or the web hosting a client already has — no repository, no build settings on the host, and only the files that changed. [How publishing works](https://sitereal.app/docs/publishing). ### Your host, your account Sign in with Netlify or Cloudflare, paste a Vercel token, or enter any FTP or SSH login. Tokens stay in your computer’s keychain, and the site goes straight to the host — never through us. ### Preview first, roll back after A preview link to send before anything goes live, the recent publishes listed, and any of them put back in one click. ### GitHub still works beside it Push to GitHub and let a host build from the repository, publish directly, or both. The site is plain Astro, so moving to another host later changes nothing in it. Questions ## Answered plainly. If something here is still unclear, the documentation goes considerably deeper. [Read the docs](https://sitereal.app/docs) ### What does it cost? Seven days free with every feature, then €69 a year — or €199 once. The two licenses give you the same application and differ only in how long they run: the lifetime license never ends, and a yearly license runs for as long as you renew it. When it ends, sitereal stops opening projects until you renew — your sites are ordinary files and keep building without it. Full details are on the pricing page. ### What exactly does it write into my project? src/pages/.astro for each page, src/components/.astro for each component, src/layouts/Layout.astro for each template, the generated stylesheets under src/styles/generated/, the small runtimes under public/scripts/, and your content and media as ordinary files. One extra file, site.sitereal, holds what the canvas knows — and the site never reads it. ### Can I hand-edit the code afterwards? Yes, and that is the point: visual editing and hand-editing are two views of the same files. Change a page, a component, a layout or a stylesheet in your editor — or let Claude Code do it — and sitereal reads it back onto the canvas. Or edit them inside sitereal: code mode puts the files beside the canvas. Nothing you write is ever written over — when the canvas changed the same file, the two are merged. ### Does it work with an existing Astro site? Yes. Point it at the folder. It adds its own files and leaves yours alone; a page you wrote by hand shows up in the page list and opens on the canvas as it is, with nothing put around it, and the ones you draw appear alongside it. ### Which platforms does it run on? macOS, Windows and Linux. ## Works with all popular site generators and frameworks

## Is Pages CMS free?

Yes, Pages CMS is 100% free, whether you want to use [the online version](https://app.pagescms.org/), deploy it for free on [Vercel](https://vercel.com/), or self-host it. It's MIT licensed through and through, feel free to extend it as you see fit.

## Do you only support GitHub?

Yes. Supposedly, we could add GitLab and Bitbucket support, but the assumption is the vast majority of users will be on GitHub. Pull requests and issues are welcome: [github.com/pages-cms/pages-cms](https://github.com/pages-cms/pages-cms).

## Why yet another CMS?

I hear you, but I needed Pages CMS to exist. I love static site generators, and while YAML front matter and Markdown aren't terribly complicated, editing content and uploading images using [GitHub.com](http://github.com/) or Git isn't really user-friendly, especially if you're updating the site with a whole team. For that reason, a lot of teams use a headless CMS like Contentful, Sanity, or Strapi. That works, but it's one more dependency and is overkill in most cases. You could also use something like Decap CMS (formerly Netlify CMS). Really cool project, but I've never been a fan of the user experience. And most importantly, I wanted something as simple as possible. Back in 2018, I had built a lightweight CMS ( [Jekyll+](https://github.com/hunvreus/jekyllplus)) with the idea of getting the CMS set up with a single configuration file. Pages CMS is the next iteration of that idea.

## Who built this?

My name is [Ronan Berder](https://ronanberder.com/) ( [@hunvreus](https://x.com/hunvreus)). I live in Singapore. I went back to writing software [after years of building (and ultimately selling) a consultancy in China](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SEzXTXo1D8I).

## I have a problem, how can I get help?

First, make sure to check the [documentation](https://pagescms.org/docs). You can also [ask for help in the Discord channel](https://pagescms.org/chat). Otherwise, [post your issue on GitHub](https://github.com/pages-cms/pages-cms).

## How can I help?

- [Sponsor me](https://github.com/sponsors/hunvreus)
- [Star the project on GitHub](https://github.com/pages-cms/pages-cms)
- [Report issues](https://github.com/pages-cms/pages-cms/issues)
- [Send pull requests](https://github.com/pages-cms/pages-cms/pulls)
- [Join the Discord chat](https://pagescms.org/chat)

Can I keep editing files in GitHub or my code editor?

Yes. After editing in GitHub or your code editor, scan the repository and rebuild the index to refresh Prosefly. Changes to Space or collection structure need scan review, and changes that conflict with a saved draft must be resolved before publication.

Can Prosefly edit any MDX component?

Visual editing supports the component syntax provided by the collection’s editor profile. Custom components and unsupported expressions remain editable in Source. Prosefly does not execute your repository code.

What happens if I stop using Prosefly?

Published files remain in your repository and can be maintained with your own tools. Your website can continue using those files through its existing build process. Unpublished drafts and media hosted by Prosefly are separate from the repository.

Does the trial require a credit card?

# The CMS for the AI era,   on your device.

Visual website builder, CMS and AI agent workspace.

No monthly fees, no lock-in, no limits.

[Download Beta](https://splitleaf.eu/download)

Mac and Windows · Try every feature free · $129 one-time license

![](https://splitleaf.eu/assets/Splitleaf---Affinity-2.png)

## A website tool that uses the real power of your computer.

Traditional content management systems live in the browser and lock your data in proprietary databases. Splitleaf doesn't.

[The CMS belongs on your device](https://splitleaf.eu/blog/on-device-cms)

## Meet your new local workspace.

### Describe the outcome.   Review every change.

### Shape HTML and CSS visuelly  without switching between tools

### Real agentic CMS,   content planned and created for you.

### Choose what ships now.   Keep the rest for later.

## Design visually.   With AI.

Click, edit, move and style elements on the canvas. Splitleaf writes clean class-based HTML and CSS directly to your project.

**The design panel you know**

Edit text, layout, spacing, appearance and typography with immediate feedback.

**\+ state-driven panel**

When AI has created a design, use the state panel to quickly see the CSS changes in a list.

**Safe by design**

Valid structures, visual undo and real files keep experimentation reversible.

## Download Splitleaf

Splitleaf runs on your Mac or Windows PC. One license unlocks the visual designer, the built-in CMS and the AI agent. No site plans, no AI credits, no feature paywalls.

### Mac

Fully native. Works on Intel and Apple silicon Macs.

[Download for Mac](https://splitleaf.eu/download/mac)

[Email download link](https://splitleaf.eu/download/mac)

Enter email and receive a download link

![The designer open on a macbook, showing the stylepanel](https://splitleaf.eu/assets/Mac-preview.png)

### Windows

Runs nice on both ARM and Intel.

[Download for Windows](https://splitleaf.eu/download/windows)

[Email download link](https://splitleaf.eu/download/windows)

Enter email and receive a download link

![The designer open on a windows computer showing the CMS](https://splitleaf.eu/assets/Windows-preview.png)

License: $129 once · Team: $6/mo per collaborator · [See pricing](https://splitleaf.eu/pay-once-own-forever)

## Any model.  With your own keys.

Connect Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter or all three. You pay the provider's price. Splitleaf runs no server between you and the model and adds no markup.

- Choose the right model for each task
- See the usage of every chat
- Keys stay outside your site folder
- Ready for Claud code

OWN YOUR CODE·PAY ONCE, OWN FOREVER·HOST WHERE YOU WANT·DESIGN OFFLINE·BUILD WITH AGENTS·OWN YOUR CODE·PAY ONCE, OWN FOREVER·HOST WHERE YOU WANT·DESIGN OFFLINE·BUILD WITH AGENTS·

## Full control of  what goes live.

We grew tired of the flawed "Publish" button that releases every change you've made.

From review to live, in one view. Splitleaf turns the full release process into a visual board your entire team can understand and manage.

Give employees and contributors access to make changes, review or publish work to the live site.

### Selective publish

Select individual pages, content, design changes or files and publish only them.

### Share the workload

Review, stage or publish coworkers' changes, and see progress.

### Git-backed

Changes made in Splitleaf are stored and tracked in GitHub, without your team having to think about it.

## Bring your existing site.

Point Splitleaf at a folder with real HTML and CSS and it becomes an editable project, structure, classes and content intact.

- Real files in, real files out

- Git history preserved, nothing rewritten

- No proprietary format to get locked into

OWN YOUR CODE·PAY ONCE, OWN FOREVER·HOST WHERE YOU WANT·DESIGN OFFLINE·BUILD WITH AGENTS·OWN YOUR CODE·PAY ONCE, OWN FOREVER·HOST WHERE YOU WANT·DESIGN OFFLINE·BUILD WITH AGENTS·

## Local website management.  Without managing custom codebases.

**Real files** HTML, CSS, JavaScript & Markdown files, not database rows**$0** Markup on your AI usage**$129** One-time license**Unlimited** Sites on one license

One person with five CMS sites pays $7,500 over five years on Webflow, at its published yearly prices. In Splitleaf that is $129 once, plus your own hosting. [Compare pricing](https://splitleaf.eu/cost-comparison)

## This site is a folder.  We built it with Splitleaf.

splitleaf.eu is a Splitleaf project. Pages, components, styles and Markdown content sit in one folder, and every publish is a Git commit.

splitleaf/

- pages/every page is an HTML file

  - \_templates/one design per collection

    - blog.htmlevery blog post

    - compare.htmlevery comparison

    - documentation.htmlevery help article

    - changelog.htmlevery release


  - for/a page per audience

    - for-agencies.html

    - for-freelancers.html

    - for-startups.html

    - organisations.html

    - eu-companies.html


  - legal/

    - privacy-policy.html

    - terms-and-conditions.html


  - index.htmlthe page you are reading

  - pricing.html

  - manifesto.html

  - blog.htmllists the posts in content/blog

  - 404.html

  - … 14 more pages

- components/built once, used on every page

  - site-navigation.htmlthe menu at the top

  - site-footer.html

  - faq-item.htmlone question, one answer

  - download-app-button.html

  - section-bottom-cta.html

  - documentation-sidebar.html


- content/the CMS, in Markdown

  - blog/19 posts

    - \_collection.jsonthe fields of a post

    - SKILL.mdhow we write, for people and agents

    - on-device-cms/

      - \_item.jsontitle, date, author

      - content.mdthe article


    - webflow-alternative/

      - \_item.jsontitle, date, author

      - content.mdthe article

      - \_brief.mdthe research behind it


    - … 17 more posts

  - compare/8 comparisons

    - \_collection.json

    - splitleaf-vs-webflow/

      - \_item.json

      - content.md

      - shortVerdict.md

      - pricingEmbed.md

      - faq.md

      - sources.md


    - … 7 more comparisons

  - documentation/18 help articles

    - \_collection.json

    - get-started-with-splitleaf/

      - \_item.json

      - content.md


    - … 17 more articles

  - changelog/one folder per release

    - \_collection.json

    - 0-2-1/the latest release

      - \_item.json

      - content.mdwhat changed


    - … 24 earlier releases

  - authors/

    - \_collection.json

    - bernt-roalkvam/

      - \_item.jsonname, photo, bio


- styles/plain CSS

  - site.cssevery class on the site

  - variables.csscolours, sizes, radii

  - fonts.css


- public/files served as they are

  - assets/images, video, logos

    - Splitleaf---Logo.svg

    - Open-graph.pngthe image a shared link shows

    - Mac-preview.png

    - flows-splitleaf-edit-review-publish.mp4

    - … and the rest of the media

  - schema/the open file format

    - config.v3.json

    - collection.v1.json

    - item.v2.json


- AGENTS.mdhouse rules for AI agents

- splitleaf.config.jsonpage list and site settings


## The questions we would ask

Why not just use Claude Code?

You can, inside Splitleaf. Claude Code runs in the agent panel on the Claude plan you already have. It works on the same files as the visual canvas, the CMS and the publish board. People who do not code can review, edit and publish. Every change is staged for you to keep or undo.

Is the AI local today?

Not yet. The agent calls the provider you connect: Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter, on your own key. Everything else is already local. The app, your files, your edits and the design work all run on your Mac or Windows PC. No server of ours sits between you and the model. Local models are the next step, and the architecture is built for them.

Is this a static site generator with a visual editor?

The output is static HTML and CSS, so that part is true. The difference is who can use it. There is no build configuration, no template language and no terminal. A designer or a marketer designs, edits content and publishes from one app.

Do I pay Splitleaf for AI?

No. You connect your own key and pay your provider at its normal price. Splitleaf runs no server between you and the model and adds no markup. The agent panel shows the usage of each chat.

Where are my API keys stored?

On Splitleaf's server in the EU, encrypted, for that one site. A key is never written to your site folder, so it never ends up in your repository.

What happens after the 12 months of updates?

The app you bought keeps working and keeps publishing. The licence includes 12 months of updates. A future major version is an optional paid upgrade.

Does it run on Mac and Windows?

Yes. Splitleaf is a native desktop app for Mac and Windows. It runs on Intel and Apple silicon Macs with macOS 11 or later, and on Intel, AMD and Arm PCs.

## Make your next site truly yours.

Start free. Design locally. Publish when you are ready.

[Download Beta](https://splitleaf.eu/download)

# Three.js hero sections and templates

Explore interactive Three.js hero sections with WebGL scenes, responsive layouts, editable source, and production-ready website templates.

- [Complete Shelf](/hero/complete-shelf-landing-page)
The complete Working Volumes bookshelf page with all seven tools, its responsive editorial interface, and authored Three.js presentation.
- [Bestsellers Book Showcase](/hero/bestsellers-book-showcase)
The complete Field Manuals book showcase, preserved unchanged with its editorial layout, authored motion, interactions, and embedded media.
- [Orrery](/hero/orrery-page)
The complete Orrery studio hero, preserved unchanged with its procedural stone plinth, luminous orbital rings, drifting debris, editorial cards, and compact dock navigation.
- [Cortexa](/hero/cortexa-page)
The complete Cortexa intelligence-platform hero, preserved unchanged with its procedural point-cloud bust, silhouette bloom, data haze, and pointer-following torch interaction.
- [Cathode — Workstation](/hero/cathode-page/workstation)
The complete Cathode hero UI around the owner's workstation revision: the isometric CRT cabinet, source-code screen, backlit keyboard, desk mouse, navigation, launch copy, and primary CTA.
- [Cathode — Console](/hero/cathode-page/console)
The complete Cathode hero UI around the living-room console variant: a side-scroller display, vented console slab, illuminated gamepad, navigation, launch copy, and primary CTA.
- [Cathode — Studio](/hero/cathode-page/studio)
The complete Cathode hero UI around the recording-studio variant: boom microphone, pop screen, desk mixer, programme monitor, ON AIR sign, navigation, launch copy, and primary CTA.
- [Cathode — Cinema](/hero/cathode-page/cinema)
The complete Cathode hero UI around the cinema variant: tripod camera rig, matte box, monitor, panel light, slate, navigation, launch copy, and primary CTA.
- [Vella Bank](/hero/vella-bank)
A full-screen banking hero led by four procedural cards, live customer balances, restrained metallic colour, and a sharp editorial product pitch built for finance and card launches.
- [Attune](/hero/attune)
The complete attune hero page, preserved unchanged with its procedural Three.js Mars, orbital telemetry, dust haze, and full-bleed product layout.
- [Betawise](/hero/betawise-globe-page)
The complete Betawise attribution page, preserved unchanged with its normal-extruded stroke globe in Three.js, its starfield and orbital arcs, and the authored WebGL2 liquid-metal CTAs.
- [Betawise](/hero/betawise-particle-page)
The complete Betawise particle-bust hero page, preserved unchanged with its Three.js point-cloud bust and pointer response. Betawise is the later full page built from the same brand.
- [Tidecrest](/hero/tidecrest-page)
The complete Tidecrest hero page, preserved unchanged with its Three.js terrain and the authored EffectComposer and UnrealBloom post-processing chain.
- [Sylva — Living Green](/hero/sylva/living-green)
The moss-root world with pale flowers, ferns, drifting pollen, the landing butterfly, and native liquid-metal controls behind the full hero layout.
- [Sylva — Sakura Sunset](/hero/sylva/sakura-sunset)
The same page and layout carrying the Sakura Sunset scene instead: mossy cherry boughs in open blossom over a golden cushion at dusk.
- [Sylva — Maple Autumn](/hero/sylva/maple-autumn)
The same page over the Maple Autumn scene: palmate leaves crimson to gold on mossy boughs, with the dock and button plates retoned to its slate dusk.
- [Sylva — Sequoia Mist](/hero/sylva/sequoia-mist)
The same page over the Sequoia Mist scene: redwood sprays on fibrous cinnamon bark, with the dock and button plates carried up into its pale grove fog.
- [Aster Halftone Bloom](/hero/halftone-bloom)
A full-screen analytics hero built around a luminous procedural rose re-photographed as a cross-shaped halftone lattice, with petal erosion, falling dust, pointer-driven light, glass controls, and restrained editorial typography.
- [Advanced Glass Material](/hero/advanced-glass-material)
A full-screen material showcase built around a faceted spectral glass form over an interactive water field, with two-bounce refraction, edge dispersion, studio reflections, pointer-driven orbit, direct glass impulses, and a restrained technical product interface.
- [Anima](/hero/anima)
A full-screen perception platform hero with a procedural point-cloud bust and headphones, layered dust, haze, stars, bloom, an entrance that settles the figure into focus while the interface resolves out of a blur one element at a time, and a localized pointer field that parts the signal around the cursor.
- [Skyfield](/hero/skyfield)
A full-screen carbon survey journey across procedural moss-covered terrain, with atmospheric cloud layers, scan telemetry, a day/night control, pointer parallax, and a scroll-scrubbed descent from observation to verified removal.
- [ThreeUI Rings](/hero/threeui-rings)
A complete ThreeUI library hero wrapped around concentric typographic rings whose glyphs melt into dots, wire into a chaotic mesh, and carry pointer-triggered ripples through the field.
- [Foldwork](/hero/foldwork)
A complete monochrome product-studio hero whose divided headline surrounds a sparkling procedural form inside a perspective grid, framed by precise navigation, availability, and contact details.
- [Meridian Slow Matter](/hero/meridian-slow-matter)
A monochrome applied-fluid hero where voxel wax drifts through a transparent vessel, framed by pixel typography, technical telemetry, selectable phases, and a tactile set-it-drifting control.
- [Everbloom](/hero/everbloom)
An image-led fantasy codex hero with a blindfolded saint-knight, procedurally tooled book cases, falling blossom and smoke layers, pointer-lit candle reveal, and a four-chapter virtual descent.
- [Aureon Markets](/hero/aureon-markets)
A polished blue-and-violet trading hero with a refractive liquid-metal market sculpture, draggable glass metrics, multilingual navigation, and fully local account-preview dialogs.
- [Quadrix](/hero/quadrix)
A copper-edged HOSHI phone floating above a terminal grid, with a live tetromino simulation, five cycling display modes, bitmap typography, pointer orbit, and inertial drag rotation.
- [Dark Souls Holo Card — The Ashen One](/hero/dark-souls-holo-card/ashen-one)
The original holographic card beside the candlelit sword shrine.
- [Dark Souls Holo Card — Cindermane](/hero/dark-souls-holo-card/cindermane)
A firelit monster card with layered holographic foil and pointer-reactive lighting.
- [Koi Mecha](/hero/koi-mecha)
Nacre's complete sculptural koi hero, with porcelain, gold, and nocturnal finishes, editorial navigation, collection dialogs, and a tactile Three.js fish study.
- [Cinder K1](/hero/cinder-k1)
A cinematic mechanical-keyboard hero with a pointer-guided lamp, responsive camera orbit, live keypress feedback, ember particles, firelit typography, and tactile pre-order controls.
- [Velara Vortex](/hero/velara-vortex)
A full-screen brand-and-motion studio hero pairing precise editorial typography with a layered ring of 12 image cards that follows an authored vortex sequence and leans into pointer engagement.
- [Tideform](/hero/tideform-page)
A complete studio hero with a radial phase-field lattice, pointer-warmed crests, click-triggered ignition rings, character-level heading reactions, and restrained editorial navigation.
- [Emberline](/hero/emberline-page)
A complete GPU orchestration hero with glass navigation, restrained editorial copy, social proof, stat cards, and a pointer-reactive blue-white vortex line field.
- [Volta Atelier](/hero/volta-atelier)
The isolated Volta Atelier opening section: an oversized typographic frame around an eleven-card, pointer-reactive studio collage with ambient dust and producer details.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is a Three.js hero section?

It is the opening section of a website with an interactive Three.js, WebGL, or shader-driven visual combined with real interface content and calls to action.

### Can I use only the 3D background from a hero?

Many heroes separate the visual scene from the surrounding interface. Check the component source and variants to see whether the background can be reused on its own.

### How do I keep a Three.js hero fast?

Control pixel ratio, geometry and particle counts, pause work when the scene is off-screen, and provide a reduced-motion or static fallback for constrained devices.

### Can the hero match an existing brand system?

Yes. The source can be adapted to your typography, colors, spacing, copy, assets, lighting, camera, and motion while preserving the core interaction.

# Components

- [Tech Text](/text-animations/tech-text)
A wordmark whose letters turn into dashed vector paths under the cursor.
- [Text Loop](/text-animations/text-loop)
A seamless text marquee that flows along curved SVG paths.
- [Masked Heading](/text-animations/masked-heading)
A headline with a drifting colour mesh or image showing through, revealed word by word.
- [Particle Text](/text-animations/particle-text)
Text assembles from drifting particles that scatter and reform on demand.
- [Split Flap Text](/text-animations/split-flap-text)
Mechanical split-flap departure board that clacks through to each new phrase.
- [Warp Text](/text-animations/warp-text)
WebGL warp that bends and refracts the text around the pointer.
- [Stroke Text](/text-animations/stroke-text)
Outlined letterforms draw themselves on, then flood with fill.
- [Depth Text](/text-animations/depth-text)
Layered extruded type with parallax that shifts against the pointer.
- [Fold Text](/text-animations/fold-text)
Lines unfold into place like creased paper opening flat.
- [Echo Text](/text-animations/echo-text)
Ghosted copies trail behind the text and settle into a single word.
- [Split Text](/text-animations/split-text)
Splits text into characters / words for staggered entrance animation.
- [Blur Text](/text-animations/blur-text)
Text starts blurred then crisply resolves for a soft-focus reveal effect.
- [Circular Text](/text-animations/circular-text)
Layouts characters around a circle with optional rotation animation.
- [Text Type](/text-animations/text-type)
Typewriter effect with blinking cursor and adjustable typing cadence.
- [Shuffle](/text-animations/shuffle)
Animated text reveal where characters shuffle before settling.
- [Shiny Text](/text-animations/shiny-text)
A sheen of light that sweeps across text, from soft bands to chrome-like reflections.
- [Text Pressure](/text-animations/text-pressure)
Characters scale / warp interactively based on pointer pressure zone.
- [Curved Loop](/text-animations/curved-loop)
Flowing looping text path along a customizable curve with drag interaction.
- [Fuzzy Text](/text-animations/fuzzy-text)
Vibrating fuzzy text with controllable hover intensity.
- [Gradient Text](/text-animations/gradient-text)
Living gradients inside your text: a sliding sweep, a drifting mesh or a swinging conic fan.
- [Falling Text](/text-animations/falling-text)
Text that breaks apart and tumbles into a pile you can drag, throw and swipe, then flies back into place.
- [Text Cursor](/text-animations/text-cursor)
Text or emoji that trails your cursor as stamped copies, a following chain or a ribbon of letters.
- [Decrypted Text](/text-animations/decrypted-text)
Hacker-style decryption cycling random glyphs until resolving to real text.
- [True Focus](/text-animations/true-focus)
Applies dynamic blur / clarity based over a series of words in order.
- [Scroll Float](/text-animations/scroll-float)
Text gently floats / parallax shifts on scroll.
- [Scroll Reveal](/text-animations/scroll-reveal)
Text gently unblurs and reveals on scroll.
- [ASCII Text](/text-animations/ascii-text)
Waving ASCII text that tilts toward the pointer, scrambles on hover and ripples on click.
- [Scrambled Text](/text-animations/scrambled-text)
Detects cursor position and applies a distortion effect to text.
- [Rotating Text](/text-animations/rotating-text)
Cycles through multiple phrases with 3D rotate / flip transitions.
- [Glitch Text](/text-animations/glitch-text)
RGB split and distortion glitch effect with jitter effects.
- [Scroll Velocity](/text-animations/scroll-velocity)
Text marquee animatio - speed and distortion scale with user's scroll velocity.
- [Variable Proximity](/text-animations/variable-proximity)
Letter styling changes continuously with pointer distance mapping.
- [Count Up](/text-animations/count-up)
Animated number counter supporting formatting and decimals.
- [Crystalized Ball](/animations/crystalized-ball)
A glass ball with a crackling electric rim and glowing dust that swirls with the cursor.
- [Electric Logo](/animations/electric-logo)
Turns any logo into a living lightning outline, with arcs that leap off its edges.
- [Dither Veil](/animations/dither-veil)
A 1-bit dithered photo the cursor burns through to full colour, knitting back cell by cell.
- [Glow Cursor](/animations/glow-cursor)
Light that pours from the cursor, drifts softly through the air and cools as it fades.
- [Scroll Expand](/animations/scroll-expand)
A rounded media frame that grows to full bleed as it scrolls through the viewport.
- [Ripple Distortion](/animations/ripple-distortion)
Pointer-driven water displacement that warps content and leaves a decaying wake.
- [Elastic Mesh](/animations/elastic-mesh)
Turns text or any logo into a puffy inflated shape you can press, poke and stretch like jelly.
- [Swarm Cursor](/animations/swarm-cursor)
A liquid swarm of particles that flows after the cursor, curls into eddies and pours around hovered buttons.
- [Halftone Reveal](/animations/halftone-reveal)
A halftone print of an image whose dots swell into the real photo under the cursor.
- [Pixel Swap](/animations/pixel-swap)
New content builds in pixel by pixel in a springy wave that starts wherever the cursor enters.
- [Cursor Grid](/animations/cursor-grid)
A crisp grid whose cells light up and fade behind the cursor, with grid styles, tiles and click pulses.
- [Animated Content](/animations/animated-content)
Wrapper that reveals its content on scroll with slides, blur, 3D tilts, soft wipes and staggered children.
- [Fade Content](/animations/fade-content)
Wrapper that fades content in on scroll, plain or out of focus, from washed-out gray, or through grain, mist and pixel blocks.
- [Electric Border](/animations/electric-border)
Wraps any element in crackling strands of current that surge near the cursor and leap off in sparks.
- [Orbit Images](/animations/orbit-images)
SVG Path customizable orbiting images effect
- [Pixel Transition](/animations/pixel-transition)
Retro pixel dissolve that covers a card in solid pixels, swaps the content underneath and clears again.
- [Glare Hover](/animations/glare-hover)
A glossy light streak that sweeps across any element in the direction the cursor moves.
- [Logo Loop](/animations/logo-loop)
Continuously looping marquee of brand or tech logos with seamless repeat and hover pause.
- [Target Cursor](/animations/target-cursor)
A reticle cursor whose corner brackets snap around targets, matching their shape.
- [Laser Flow](/animations/laser-flow)
A beam of light that splashes onto your content and pours over its corners.
- [Ghost Cursor](/animations/ghost-cursor)
A ghost of glowing smoke that floats after the cursor and curls away as it rises.
- [Gradual Blur](/animations/gradual-blur)
Progressive edge blur for headers, footers, captions and carousels, with an optional fade to color that hides at the ends of a scroll.
- [Click Spark](/animations/click-spark)
Bursts of sparks at every click, as dashes, comets, dots or stars, that can spill around buttons.
- [Magnet](/animations/magnet)
Elements magnetically ease toward the cursor then settle back with spring physics.
- [Strands](/animations/strands)
Spectral strands that twist inside a frosted glass orb and swell into a smooth bulge where they come together, like the new Siri.
- [Sticker Peel](/animations/sticker-peel)
A die-cut sticker you can peel at any edge, drag, throw and swing, in gloss, matte or holographic finishes.

[... middle omitted — see footer ...]

- [Dither](/backgrounds/dither)
Retro dithered waves with Bayer, halftone, line and noise patterns, palettes and cursor trails.
- [Faulty Terminal](/backgrounds/faulty-terminal)
A flickering CRT terminal of glowing glyphs, with phosphor trails under the cursor and glitches on click.
- [Ripple Grid](/backgrounds/ripple-grid)
A crisp grid that ripples like water, bending and lighting up as waves pass through it.
- [Dot Field](/backgrounds/dot-field)
A gradient dot field seen through a lens that follows the cursor, magnifying, pinching or swirling the dots.
- [Dot Grid](/backgrounds/dot-grid)
A springy dot grid that the cursor flicks and drags through like jelly, with click shockwaves.
- [Threads](/backgrounds/threads)
Flowing threads that fray apart and part around the cursor, from fine silk to contour lines.
- [Hyperspeed](/backgrounds/hyperspeed)
Night highway of glowing light trails on a winding road that warps into hyperspace while you hold.
- [Iridescence](/backgrounds/iridescence)
Liquid iridescent surface with shifting folds that you can stir with the cursor.
- [Waves](/backgrounds/waves)
Dense flowing lines that sway like silk, bend around the cursor and spring back into place.
- [Magnet Lines](/backgrounds/magnet-lines)
A field of magnetic lines that swing toward the cursor, ripple outward and spin with every click.
- [Grid Distortion](/backgrounds/grid-distortion)
Image background that breaks into a grid of blocks under the cursor and settles back into place.
- [Ballpit](/backgrounds/ballpit)
A soft-lit pit of physics balls you can shove with the cursor, grab, throw and blast apart.
- [Orb](/backgrounds/orb)
A glowing ring of swirling color that breathes, trails an orbiting light and reaches toward the cursor.
- [Letter Glitch](/backgrounds/letter-glitch)
A calm field of letters that flicker, scramble and glitch in color, stirred by the cursor and torn by clicks.
- [Grid Motion](/backgrounds/grid-motion)
A tilted wall of drifting tiles that slides with the pointer and lights up where it rests.
- [Shape Grid](/backgrounds/shape-grid)
A drifting grid of shapes that lights up under the cursor, with perspective tilt and rainbow trails.
- [Liquid Chrome](/backgrounds/liquid-chrome)
Soft ribbons of liquid chrome that swirl through a dark pool, ripple under the cursor and catch the light as it moves.
- [Balatro](/backgrounds/balatro)
The swirling Balatro paint shader, with crisp pixels, a cursor that stirs the paint and click whirlpools.

# Anti-Patterns

 57 named patterns across 10 categories. Deceptive design, addictive mechanics, accessibility weaponization, and common UX failures. Each one identified, categorized, and rated.

| Pattern | Severity | Description | Category |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bait and Switch | Critical | Offers one thing, delivers another. User clicks expecting X, gets Y. | Deceptive Patterns |
| Trick Questions | Critical | Uses double negatives, confusing phrasing, or inverted logic so users select the opposite of their intent. | Deceptive Patterns |
| Visual Misdirection | High | Uses size, color, contrast, or positioning to make the business-preferred option look like the only option or the default. | Deceptive Patterns |
| Disguised Ads | High | Makes advertisements look like content, navigation, or system UI. | Deceptive Patterns |
| Hidden Costs | Critical | Reveals fees, taxes, or charges only at the final step of a purchase flow. | Deceptive Patterns |
| Sneak into Basket | Critical | Adds items, insurance, warranties, or donations to a cart without explicit user action. | Deceptive Patterns |
| Confirmshaming | High | Uses guilt, shame, or social pressure in opt-out copy ("No thanks, I don't want to save money"). | Deceptive Patterns |
| Prechecked Consent | Critical | Pre-selects checkboxes for marketing, data sharing, or terms the user hasn't reviewed. | Prechecked & Default Manipulation |
| Opt-Out Burden | Critical | Makes opting out require significantly more effort than opting in (multi-page flows, phone calls, postal mail). | Prechecked & Default Manipulation |
| Privacy Zuckering | High | Defaults to maximum data exposure, relying on users not changing settings. Named after Facebook's repeated defaults. | Prechecked & Default Manipulation |
| Forced Continuity | Critical | Auto-enrolls users in paid subscriptions after free trials without clear warning or easy cancellation. | Prechecked & Default Manipulation |
| Default to Most Expensive | Medium | Pre-selects the highest-cost tier or option in pricing selectors. | Prechecked & Default Manipulation |
| Fake Countdown Timers | Critical | Displays timers that reset, have no real deadline, or create false urgency. | Urgency & Scarcity Fabrication |
| Fabricated Scarcity | Critical | Claims limited availability ("Only 2 left!") that doesn't reflect actual inventory. | Urgency & Scarcity Fabrication |
| Fake Social Proof | Critical | Displays fabricated activity notifications ("15 people viewing this now") or fake reviews. | Urgency & Scarcity Fabrication |
| Pressure Selling | High | Uses time-limited "exclusive" offers designed to prevent comparison shopping. | Urgency & Scarcity Fabrication |
| Loss Framing | Medium | Frames choices as losses ("You're losing $50/month by not upgrading") rather than gains, to exploit loss aversion. | Urgency & Scarcity Fabrication |
| Infinite Scroll | Medium | Removes natural stopping points to maximize session length. No pagination, no "end," no sense of completion. | Addictive Design |
| Variable Ratio Reinforcement | High | Uses unpredictable rewards (likes, notifications, content) to trigger dopamine-driven checking behavior. Slot machine mechanics. | Addictive Design |
| Streak Manipulation | High | Creates artificial loss consequences for missing daily engagement ("Your 30-day streak will be lost!"). | Addictive Design |
| Pull-to-Refresh Gambling | Medium | Makes content refresh feel like pulling a slot machine lever — will there be something new? | Addictive Design |
| Autoplay Chains | Medium | Automatically starts next content without consent, exploiting inertia to extend sessions. | Addictive Design |
| Artificial Incompleteness | Medium | Shows progress bars or "profile completeness" scores that exploit completion bias to extract more data or engagement. | Addictive Design |
| Permission Harassment | High | Repeatedly asks for permissions (notifications, location, contacts) after user has declined. | Attention Exploitation |
| Notification Spam | High | Sends excessive, low-value notifications to pull users back into the product. | Attention Exploitation |
| Obstruction Interstitials | High | Blocks content with full-screen overlays, newsletter signups, or app-install prompts that are difficult to dismiss. | Attention Exploitation |
| Attention Bait | Medium | Uses misleading notification badges, unread counts, or red dots to manufacture urgency. | Attention Exploitation |
| Nagging | Medium | Persistent prompts to rate, review, share, upgrade, or complete actions the user has shown no interest in. | Attention Exploitation |
| Inaccessible Unsubscribe | Critical | Makes cancellation or opt-out flows fail with screen readers, keyboard navigation, or other assistive tools. | Accessibility Weaponized |
| CAPTCHA as Gatekeeping | High | Uses CAPTCHA challenges that are disproportionately difficult for users with disabilities, without providing accessible alternatives. | Accessibility Weaponized |
| Low-Contrast Opt-Out | High | Makes opt-out links or decline buttons deliberately low-contrast, tiny, or visually suppressed. | Accessibility Weaponized |
| Assistive Technology Traps | Critical | Creates keyboard focus traps or reading-order manipulation that confuses assistive tech in the area of consent or cancellation flows. | Accessibility Weaponized |
| Child-Targeted Manipulation | Critical | Uses game-like mechanics, character appeals, or peer pressure to drive purchases or data collection from children. | Vulnerable User Exploitation |
| Elderly-Targeted Confusion | Critical | Exploits lower digital literacy with complex flows, jargon-heavy interfaces, or hidden cancellation paths. | Vulnerable User Exploitation |
| Crisis Exploitation | Critical | Takes advantage of users in urgent situations (medical, financial, legal) with high-pressure tactics or inflated pricing. | Vulnerable User Exploitation |
| Addiction Exploitation | Critical | Targets users with known addictive behaviors (gambling, shopping, social media) with triggering mechanics. | Vulnerable User Exploitation |
| Financial Vulnerability Targeting | Critical | Offers predatory financial products with deliberately obscured terms to users showing financial stress signals. | Vulnerable User Exploitation |
| Anthropomorphic Manipulation | High | Gives AI human-like emotional responses to make users feel guilt, attachment, or obligation toward the system. | AI-Specific Dark Patterns |
| Opaque Personalization | High | Uses recommendation algorithms to create filter bubbles or steer choices without the user understanding why they see what they see. | AI-Specific Dark Patterns |
| Manufactured Dependency | High | Designs AI assistance to reduce user competence over time, making them dependent on the tool. | AI-Specific Dark Patterns |
| Simulated Understanding | Medium | Makes AI appear to understand context, emotion, or intent it cannot actually process, creating false trust. | AI-Specific Dark Patterns |
| Algorithmic Exploitation | Critical | Uses behavioral data to identify and exploit individual psychological vulnerabilities at scale. | AI-Specific Dark Patterns |
| Undisclosed AI Decisions | High | Hides the fact that an AI is making consequential decisions (pricing, eligibility, content ranking) from the user. | AI-Specific Dark Patterns |
| Dead Ends | Medium | Flows that terminate without guidance — empty states with no actions, error pages with no recovery path. | Common UX Failures |

[... middle omitted — see footer ...]

| Destructive Defaults | High | Irreversible actions (delete, publish, send) that are too easy to trigger accidentally. | Common UX Failures |
| Broken Error Recovery | High | Error messages that don't explain what went wrong or how to fix it. "An error occurred." | Common UX Failures |
| Assumption of Context | Medium | Expects the user to remember information from previous screens, sessions, or channels. | Common UX Failures |
| Mobile Afterthought | High | Desktop-first design that becomes cramped, broken, or missing features on mobile. | Common UX Failures |
| Real Estate Tour | Medium | Design documentation or rationale that describes what's on screen ("there's a button in the top left with rounded corners") instead of explaining why it's there and what problem it solves. Inventory masquerading as intent. | Common UX Failures |
| Smoothed-arc Personas | High | Constructs a single user narrative arc that smooths over real variance in research. The persona reads coherently when the underlying data showed three or more distinct, non-converging user paths. The team empathizes with a fictional composite, not actual users. | Narrative Pathologies in Design Process |
| Manufactured-Tension Briefs | High | Strategic narratives whose complication is sized to fit a predetermined resolution rather than what evidence shows. Symptom: the tension feels conveniently shaped. Result: teams commit to strategies built on inflated or invented problems. | Narrative Pathologies in Design Process |
| Conflict-Default Journeys | Medium | Frames every user experience as a hero's journey with a goal, obstacle, and resolution — even when the actual experience is habit-shaped, ambient, or recurring. Forces conflict structure onto experiences that don't have it, distorting the design. | Narrative Pathologies in Design Process |
| Story-as-Evidence Substitution | High | Uses narrative emotional appeal to win stakeholder assent for design decisions that aren't supported by research. The story carries the conviction; the evidence is post-hoc or absent. | Narrative Pathologies in Design Process |
| Choreography Role-Reduction | Medium | Service blueprints that flatten humans into system roles. The blueprint reads cleanly because nobody is in it — the customer, the agent, the system are all abstractions. Coordination clarity purchased by erasing the people the service exists for. | Narrative Pathologies in Design Process |

# Cauldron OS - v0.50 Release Plan

> **Created:** 16 July 2026
> **Status:** ✅ Complete - merged to `main` as v0.50.0 (PR #21, merge `8f84355`)
> **Repo:** `/Users/habibi/hermes/apps-codebases/cauldron-os/`
> **Release theme:** Verification, handoff quality and design-system export

## Goal

Make Cauldron OS prove that a generated project is usable before handing it over.

The release borrows the useful parts of BuilderOS without installing BuilderOS or creating a second orchestration layer.

## Current baseline

Cauldron already has:

- 7-stage pipeline: Brain Dump -> Interrogate -> Design System -> Blueprint -> Prototype -> Build -> Export
- Blueprint version history and diffing
- Prototype quality scoring and critique/refinement loop
- Multi-agent handoff packages
- Community design-system and scaffold imports
- Sandboxed XML build agent with SSE progress
- Scaffold export and `cauldron.project.json`

The current working tree has five uncommitted files. Preserve and inspect those changes before starting this release. Do not overwrite unrelated work.

## Release scope

### Phase 0 - Baseline and contracts

**Purpose:** establish a clean starting point before feature work.

- [x] Inspect and classify the five existing modified files.
- [x] Confirm whether the current deep-research test change belongs in the release branch.
- [x] Read `docs/PUBLIC_INTERFACES.md` and update it before changing public response shapes.
- [x] Create a release branch from the verified current state.
- [x] Record baseline results: `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`.

**Files likely touched:**

- `docs/PUBLIC_INTERFACES.md`
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`
- `package.json`
- `CHANGELOG.md`

**Gate:** existing tests pass and unrelated dirty work is understood, not silently discarded.

### Phase 1 - Build Verification Pass

**Purpose:** add an explicit post-build quality gate rather than stopping when files exist.

Add a Cauldron-native verification contract after `/api/build/generate` and `/api/build/refine`.

The pass should:

1. Inspect the generated workspace manifest and entrypoint.
2. Run the declared install/build/test commands when available.
3. Run safe static checks for HTML structure, missing assets, broken local references and obvious placeholder content.
4. Run accessibility checks that work locally without requiring a paid service.
5. Capture stdout, stderr, exit code, duration and command for every check.
6. Return a structured result: `passed`, `failed`, `skipped` or `not_configured`.
7. Display a clear overall result: `PASS`, `PASS WITH WARNINGS` or `BLOCKED`.
8. Allow the user to send the findings back into the build agent for a fix pass.

**Suggested implementation surfaces:**

- `lib/verification.js` - pure verification runner and result normalisation
- `routes/build.js` - verification endpoint and build-session integration
- `routes/projects.js` - persist the final verification summary in the handoff package
- `public/index.html` - Verification panel and result states
- `public/scripts/app.js` - verification state, progress and fix-again action
- `docs/PUBLIC_INTERFACES.md` - response contract
- `tests/verification-smoke.js` - passing, failing and skipped checks

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A generated static project can be verified from inside Cauldron.
- A failing check is visible and does not appear as success.
- Missing commands produce `not_configured`, not a false pass.
- The result survives export in `cauldron.project.json` and `README.md`.
- The user can request a fix pass using the captured findings.
- Existing local and cloud build paths remain available.

### Phase 2 - Generated Launch Checklist

**Purpose:** make every exported project understandable to a human.

Generate `launch-checklist.md` in the exported project package.

It should include:

- project name and generated date
- selected template and entrypoint
- install, development and production commands
- required environment variables, without secrets
- verification results and skipped checks
- known limitations and warnings
- human actions still required
- a short "you'll know it worked when..." test
- links to `blueprint.md`, `prototype.html`, `design-system.md` and `cauldron.project.json`

**Suggested implementation surfaces:**

- `lib/handoff-package.js`
- `routes/projects.js`
- `routes/build-agents.js`
- `tests/handoff-smoke.js`
- `tests/scaffold-export-smoke.js`

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Every successful handoff includes the checklist.
- The checklist reflects the selected scaffold rather than generic commands.
- Secrets and API-key values never appear in the generated file.
- Handoff smoke tests verify the file contents and links.

### Phase 3 - Optional Design System Package

**Purpose:** turn Cauldron's selected design reference into a reusable human/agent contract.

Add an opt-in export containing:

- `docs/design.md` - machine-readable tokens plus rationale
- `docs/design.html` - self-contained human-readable style guide

The export must be derived from the selected design reference and the generated prototype where possible. It must not invent a token system that contradicts the actual output.

Include at minimum:

- colour tokens
- typography
- spacing
- radii
- borders/elevation
- component states
- accessibility notes
- known tokens that could not be inferred

**Suggested implementation surfaces:**

- `lib/design-system-export.js`
- `routes/models-design.js` or `routes/projects.js`
- `public/index.html` - export toggle
- `public/scripts/app.js` - export request/state
- `tests/design-system-export-smoke.js`

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Export is optional and does not change the existing pipeline.
- `design.md` and `design.html` agree on the same tokens.
- The HTML guide opens without a build step or external dependency.
- Exported values are traceable to the selected reference or prototype.

### Phase 4 - Release hardening

- [x] Run the full test suite, including new verification and export tests.
- [x] Run lint and format checks.
- [x] Test local Ollama and cloud model paths where available.
- [x] Test a static HTML export and one package-based scaffold.
- [x] Test passing, failing and unavailable verification commands.
- [x] Update `README.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/PUBLIC_INTERFACES.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
- [x] Capture screenshots of the Verification panel and exported checklist.
- [x] Update package version to `0.50.0` only after all gates pass.
- [x] Open a PR for review. Do not deploy or push directly to `main`.

## Verified release result

- **GitHub:** `cre8tivoz/cauldron-os`
- **PR:** #21, merged 16 July 2026
- **Merge commit:** `8f84355`
- **Tag:** `v0.50.0`
- **Local main:** clean and equal to `origin/main`
- **Contributor fork:** `cre8tivoz/cauldron-os:main` fast-forwarded to the same commit (`8f84355`)
- **Local tracking:** `main` now tracks canonical `origin/main`
- **Tests:** `npm test` passed, including verification and design-system export smoke tests
- **Lint:** passed with 35 existing warnings and 0 errors
- **Format:** `npm run format:check` passed
- **Generated launch checklist:** included in exported handoff packages, not stored as a repository-root file

## Explicitly out of scope

- Installing BuilderOS into Hermes or Cauldron.
- Replacing Cauldron's 7-stage pipeline with BuilderOS's Product Planner.
- Replacing Blueprint as the central project contract.
- Multi-user collaboration.
- Desktop app packaging.
- Plugin marketplace or arbitrary third-party code execution.
- Automatic deployment to production.
- A second independent project-management or memory system.

## Risks and controls

| Risk | Control |
|---|---|
| Verification runs unsafe commands | Only run commands declared by the generated scaffold, inside the existing workspace sandbox, with timeouts and output limits. |
| A failed check blocks useful work | Show warnings and allow an explicit fix/refine pass; distinguish `failed` from `not_configured`. |
| Generated design docs drift from the prototype | Derive tokens from selected references and actual prototype data; label uncertain values. |
| More documents create competing sources of truth | Blueprint remains canonical. Launch checklist and design exports are derived artefacts. |
| Existing dirty work is lost | Classify the five modified files before branching or editing. Preserve unrelated changes. |
| Release scope expands into a rewrite | Keep the three deliverables: verification, launch checklist, optional design package. Park everything else. |

## Definition of done

Cauldron OS v0.50 is ready when a user can generate or build a project, run a visible verification pass, understand any failures, export a launch checklist, optionally export a design-system package, and receive a handoff whose claims are backed by captured results.

## Recommended execution order

1. Phase 0 baseline and interface contract.
2. Phase 1 Verification Pass.
3. Phase 2 Launch Checklist.
4. Phase 3 Design System Package only if Phases 1-2 remain clean and focused.
5. Phase 4 QA, documentation and PR.
