# Cauldron OS — Local-First AI Blueprint & Prototype Generator

> *Created 2026-06-03 by Claudia — last updated 2026-07-16 (v0.50.0 merged — PR #21, `8f84355` on `main`)*
> **Codebase:** `~/hermes/apps-codebases/cauldron-os/`
> **Repo:** `github.com/cre8tivoz/cauldron-os` (public, MIT)
> **Status:** 🟢 v0.50.0 released — merged to `main`; local clone synced and verified
> **Stack:** Node.js/Express 5 · AlpineJS 3 · sql.js · Playwright · HTML/CSS
> **Workflow rule:** Feature work goes branch → PR → merge. Keep `CHANGELOG.md` with each release.

GITHUB REPO: https://github.com/cre8tivoz/cauldron-os

---

## 🚀 How to Launch

```bash
cd ~/hermes/apps-codebases/cauldron-os
npm install
npm start
# → Open http://localhost:3000
```

No build step, no bundler, no signing — it's a plain Node.js + AlpineJS web app. Edit `public/index.html`, `public/scripts/app.js`, and `public/styles/app.css` and refresh the browser.

**Ollama:** For local AI generation, have Ollama running. Cloud fallback via OpenAI/Google AI Studio API keys set in the browser UI.

---

## What it is

Cauldron OS is a **local-first, design-aware AI blueprint and prototype generator**. Drop in a rough app or website idea, choose a model or design reference, and Cauldron turns the mess into a structured product blueprint with architecture notes, schema ideas, and a live HTML + AlpineJS prototype preview.

**Key differentiators:**
- **7-stage deterministic pipeline** — Brain Dump → Interrogate → Design System → Blueprint → Prototype → Build → Export. No other tool has this structured flow.
- **Annoying PM Mode / Interrogate** — unique interrogation layer that asks project-manager questions before generation.
- **Taste Engine** — Impeccable Taste anti-slop mandates + Design Reference Selector (22 brands) + Refero deep search.
- **Editable blueprint** — review and edit the generated blueprint before committing to prototype generation.
- **Local-first, BYOK cloud** — Ollama local, or OpenAI/Google AI Studio with keys stored in browser localStorage.
- **Clone and deploy** — single `npm install && npm start`, no accounts, no cloud lock-in.

---

## Codebase mapping

| Layer | What | Where |
|-------|------|-------|
| **Server** | Express 5 composition root — routes, model proxy, prompt builder, research, build pipeline | `server.js` (~805 LOC) |
| **Routes** | 14 route modules (build, drafts, generation, history, models-design, projects, proxy, research-history, spa-catchall, status, templates, workspace-preview) | `routes/*.js` |
| **Frontend** | AlpineJS SPA — pipeline UI, prototype preview, settings, draft management | `public/index.html` + `public/scripts/app.js` |
| **Styles** | Dark cyberpunk theme — tokens + app CSS | `public/styles/tokens.css` + `public/styles/app.css` |
| **Templates** | 4 scaffold targets (Static HTML, HTML+AlpineJS, Next.js, Astro) — each with promptBias + file list | `server.js` — `TEMPLATES` constant |
| **Design systems** | 22 curated brand references (Cursor, Vercel, Linear, Stripe, Apple, etc.) + Refero API deep search | `server.js` — `DESIGN_SYSTEMS` + `routes/models-design.js` |
| **Build system** | Sandboxed workspace, agent loop, file tree, handoff to export | `routes/build.js`, `lib/agent-loop.js`, `lib/workspace.js` |
| **DB** | Local sql.js — drafts, research history, build status, project overrides | `db/index.js` |
| **Docs** | README, CHANGELOG, ARCHITECTURE, CONTRIBUTING, DESIGN_REFERENCE | `docs/*.md`, `README.md` |
| **CI** | GitHub Actions — smoke tests (server health, model routing, static files) | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` |

---

## v0.50.0 — Verification & Handoff Quality ✅

**Merged:** 16 July 2026 via PR #21 (`8f84355`), tagged `v0.50.0`.

## Product Plan — v0.30 Roadmap

Detailed plan at: `docs/chasing version 0.30.md` (in the repo)

### Phase 1 — Design Systems Catalog (22 → 150+)
Bulk import Open Design's `design-systems/` directory. Add token validation schema. Instant 7x catalog boost. **Estimated: 1-2 hours.**

### Phase 2 — Agent Build Mode
Replace the stub Build stage with a real BYOK/CLI execution pipeline. When user hits "Start Build," Cauldron generates a handoff package and invokes the user's agent CLI (Cursor, Claude Code, Hermes, etc.). Stolen from Open Design's execution model. **Estimated: 4-6 hours.**

### Phase 3 — Critique & Review Loop
After prototype generation, allow natural-language feedback ("make the header bigger") and regenerate in-place. Iteration history with diff comparison. **Estimated: 6-8 hours.**

### Phase 4 — UI Polish
Progress bars with ETA, contextual empty states (onboarding prompts instead of "Nothing brewed yet"), toast hierarchy, keyboard shortcuts, settings modal with connection testing. **Estimated: 4-6 hours.**

### Phase 5 — Scaffold Export
Next.js/Astro exports create real, runnable project structures (not just biased prompts). Agent handoff generates a complete spec + invokes the user's CLI. **Estimated: 6-8 hours.**

---

## Known Issues / Technical Debt

| Issue | Status | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|
| Design systems catalog only has 22 entries | ✅ Resolved | v0.40/v0.50 catalog now includes 150+ local systems plus Refero and community imports |
| Build stage is a stub | ✅ Resolved | Sandboxed XML build loop, SSE progress, refine/stop controls and multi-agent handoff are active |
| No critique/review loop | ✅ Resolved | Prototype quality scoring plus natural-language critique/refinement are active |
| UI is functional but not polished | 🟡 Ongoing | Core pipeline is released; further visual polish remains maintenance work |
| Scaffold templates don't scaffold | ✅ Resolved | Static HTML, Alpine, Next.js and Astro scaffold export contracts are active |
| Prototype iframe content can have CSS issues | 🟡 Ongoing | Generated HTML quality still depends on model output; Verification Pass now surfaces issues |
| No multi-model per pipeline stage UI | 📝 Not scoped | Backend supports it (`stageModels` config) but frontend doesn't expose it |

---

## Configuration Reference

| Env / Setting | Default | Description |
|---------------|---------|-------------|
| `PORT` | 3000 | Server port |
| `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:11434` | Ollama endpoint |
| API keys | Browser localStorage | Set in Settings → API keys |
| Provider | Gemini (default), OpenAI-compatible | Switch in top bar |

---

## Design Decisions & Philosophy

**Why no bundler/framework?** — Cauldron is intentionally a plain Node.js + AlpineJS app. Zero build step means instant startup, no node_modules churn, and the codebase is accessible to anyone who knows HTML/CSS/JS. The trade-off is manual CSS management instead of Tailwind utility classes — worth it for the accessibility.

**Why AlpineJS?** — Reactive enough for the two-panel SPA, simple enough to not need a build step. No JSX, no virtual DOM, no state management library. Just `x-data`, `x-model`, `x-show`, and `x-text`.

**Why a deterministic 7-stage pipeline?** — One-shot generation produces slop. Forcing the user through Brain Dump → Interrogate → Taste → Blueprint → Prototype → Build → Export means each stage has a clear input, a clear output, and a clear quality gate. This is Cauldron's moat.

**Local-first over cloud-first** — No accounts, no servers, no vendor lock-in. The app runs from a `node server.js`. Data stays in `data/` (gitignored). Cloud keys are BYOK and stored in browser localStorage only.

# Cauldron OS — Bidirectional Agent Integration Scope

**Date:** 2026-07-24
**Status:** Investigation / Scoping
**Requested by:** Billy
**Author:** Claudia

---

## Context

Cauldron OS v0.50 is a local-first, design-aware product factory. It runs as a Node.js Express server on localhost:3000 with a browser SPA frontend. The pipeline is: Clarify → Blueprint → Prototype → Quality Score → Critique → Build → Export.

The tool currently has a **unidirectional agent integration** — it detects installed coding agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Hermes, OpenCode), generates scoped handoff packages, and spawns them as detached processes. There is no feedback loop. The agent runs, logs to `build.log`, and Cauldron shrugs.

This scope document investigates what it would take to make agent integration **bidirectional** — Cauldron sends a handoff, the agent builds, and Cauldron receives the results back.

---

## Current Architecture (What Exists)

### Agent Detection & Launch (`lib/build-agents.js`)
- Scans PATH via `which`/`where` for: `claude`, `codex`, `cursor`, `hermes`, `opencode`
- Each agent has a `launch` type: `run-prompt` (spawns CLI) or `open-project` (opens editor)
- `launchBuildAgent()` spawns the CLI as a **detached child process** with stdout/stderr piped to `build.log`
- Returns `{ launched, pid, command, logPath }` — fire and forget

### Handoff Package (`lib/handoff-package.js`)
- Generates a structured folder per agent with scoped files:
  - `blueprint.md` — product specification
  - `prototype.html` — HTML/AlpineJS prototype
  - `design-system.md` — selected design reference
  - `agent-prompt.md` — tailored prompt for the specific agent
  - `cauldron.project.json` — machine-readable manifest
  - `launch-checklist.md` — human runbook
  - `.cursorrules`, `.opencode/config.md` — agent-specific config
- Agent scopes are defined in `AGENT_SCOPES` (cursor=frontend, codex=architecture, claude=review, etc.)
- Multi-agent orchestration creates subdirectories under `agents/`

### Build Status Monitoring (`server.js` lines 741-818)
- `getBuildStatus()` scans the `projects/` directory
- Classifies projects by: running, stalled, completed, needs_review, unknown
- Uses `ps -axo` to detect running processes matching project paths
- Reads tail of `opencode-handoff.log` / `opencode-resume.log` for status signals
- Status overrides can be set manually via `db.setProjectStatusOverride()`

### Internal Agent Loop (`lib/agent-loop.js`)
- Full XML tool-calling agent using Ollama API (local) or cloud APIs (OpenAI/Gemini)
- Tools: `write_file`, `read_file`, `edit_file`, `delete_file`, `list_files`, `run_bash`
- Up to 40 rounds of tool calls with streaming SSE to the browser
- This is the "build" pipeline — it works and is well-tested

### Routes (`routes/build-agents.js`)
- `GET /api/build-agents` — returns detected agents
- `POST /api/build-agents/run` — creates handoff + launches agent(s)
- Returns `{ pid, logPath, command, projectPath }` — no streaming, no callback

---

## The Gaps (What's Missing)

### Gap 1: No Agent Output Capture
**Current:** Agent stdout/stderr goes to `build.log` as a fire-and-forget stream.
**Needed:** Capture agent output in structured form — tokens, tool calls, file changes, completion status.
**Why:** Without this, Cauldron can't tell the user what the agent actually did.

### Gap 2: No Completion Detection
**Current:** `getBuildStatus()` uses `ps` scanning and log tail heuristics (regex matching for "done", "completed", "error").
**Needed:** Deterministic completion signal — agent writes a completion marker, or Cauldron monitors the process exit.
**Why:** The current heuristic approach is fragile. Different agents have different output patterns.

### Gap 3: No Live Status in Browser
**Current:** The browser SPA has no way to poll or stream agent status in real time.
**Needed:** SSE or WebSocket endpoint that streams agent progress to the frontend.
**Why:** The user has no visibility into what the agent is doing after launch.

### Gap 4: No Result Ingestion
**Current:** When the agent finishes, Cauldron doesn't know what files were created or modified.
**Needed:** Post-build scan of the project directory to detect changes, or agent writes a structured result manifest.
**Why:** Without this, there's no way to show "here's what was built" or trigger the next pipeline step.

### Gap 5: No Re-engagement Loop
**Current:** Single shot — launch agent, done.
**Needed:** Ability to send follow-up prompts to a running agent, or re-launch with refined instructions.
**Why:** Real builds are iterative. One-shot handoff rarely produces final output.

---

## Proposed Solution: Three Integration Tiers

### Tier 1: Process Monitoring (Low effort, high value)
**Effort:** 1-2 days
**What:** Enhance existing `build-agents.js` to track child process lifecycle.

Changes:
1. **Don't detach the child process.** Keep a reference to `child.pid` and listen to `exit` event.
2. **Capture stdout/stderr incrementally** — parse agent output as it streams, extract structured signals.
3. **Write a `build-result.json`** when the process exits: `{ status, duration, exitCode, filesChanged, output }`.
4. **Add `GET /api/build-agents/status/:projectId`** — returns live status from the in-memory process tracker.
5. **Frontend polling** — the existing build status UI polls this endpoint every 5s.

Files to modify:
- `lib/build-agents.js` — refactor `launchBuildAgent()` to return a managed process handle
- `routes/build-agents.js` — add status endpoint, store active processes in a Map
- `public/scripts/app.js` — add polling for agent status on the build screen

Key decisions:
- Which agent output signals to parse (Claude Code uses markdown, Codex uses plain text, etc.)
- Whether to keep detached mode as a fallback for agents that don't play nice with attached processes

### Tier 2: Structured Handoff Result (Medium effort, completes the loop)
**Effort:** 3-5 days
**What:** Agent writes a structured result manifest that Cauldron can ingest.

Changes:
1. **Extend `agent-prompt.md`** to include: "When complete, write `build-result.json` with: summary, filesCreated, filesModified, errors, nextSteps."
2. **Add a post-build scanner** that walks the project directory after agent completion, diffs against the handoff snapshot, and records what changed.
3. **Ingest results into the build status DB** — update the draft record with agent output.
4. **Show results in the browser** — "Agent completed. 12 files created, 3 modified. View diff."

Files to modify:
- `lib/handoff-package.js` — extend `buildAgentPrompt()` with result manifest instructions
- New: `lib/agent-result-scanner.js` — post-build directory diff
- `routes/build-agents.js` — add result ingestion endpoint
- `db/index.js` — add agent_results table or extend drafts
- `public/scripts/app.js` — results display in project view

### Tier 3: Live Agent Streaming (High effort, full parity with T3 Code)
**Effort:** 7-10 days
**What:** Real-time streaming of agent output to the browser via SSE.

Changes:
1. **Use `child_process.spawn` with piped stdio** (not detached).
2. **Parse agent output incrementally** — extract tokens, tool calls, file operations as they happen.
3. **SSE endpoint** that streams structured events: `{ type: 'token'|'tool_call'|'file_change'|'status', data }`.
4. **Frontend renders a live build panel** — shows agent thinking, tool calls, files being written.
5. **Support interactive follow-up** — user can type a follow-up prompt while agent is running.

This is essentially what `routes/build.js` already does for the internal agent loop — the same SSE pattern applied to external CLIs.

Files to modify:
- `lib/build-agents.js` — full rewrite to managed process with streaming
- New: `lib/agent-output-parser.js` — parse CLI-specific output formats
- `routes/build-agents.js` — SSE streaming endpoint
- `public/scripts/app.js` — live build panel UI
- Multiple: agent-specific output format handlers (Claude, Codex, etc.)

---

## Recommendation

**Start with Tier 1.** It's 1-2 days of work, uses existing patterns (SSE streaming is already proven in `routes/build.js`), and closes the most critical gap — knowing whether the agent finished or died.

Tier 2 is worth doing alongside Tier 1 since the prompt changes are trivial.

Tier 3 is a v2 feature. Only worth it if Cauldron becomes an active tool again. The internal agent loop already provides the live streaming experience for local builds — Tier 3 would extend that to external agents.

**Total estimated effort:**
- Tier 1 + 2: 4-7 days (one sprint)
- Tier 3: additional 7-10 days (separate sprint, only if needed)

---

## Architecture Constraints

1. **No Tauri/Electron required.** All of this works within the existing Node.js + browser architecture. The Express server already manages child processes and streams SSE — this is extending that pattern.

2. **No Apple Developer account needed.** The tool runs on localhost. No code signing, no notarisation, no distribution headaches.

3. **Agent CLI compatibility.** Different agents output different formats. The parser needs to handle:
   - Claude Code: markdown with tool use blocks
   - Codex: plain text with function call markers
   - Cursor: opens editor, no CLI output to capture (Tier 3 only — Tier 1 treats it as fire-and-forget)
   - OpenCode: terminal-native output
   - Hermes: structured tool output (we control this one)

4. **Process isolation.** Each agent build runs in its own project directory. No shared state between concurrent builds. The existing `buildSessions` Map handles this.

5. **Backward compatible.** The handoff-only mode (no agent launch) continues to work unchanged. Bidirectional integration is opt-in per agent.

---

## What This Would Mean for Cauldron

If Tier 1 + 2 ship, Cauldron becomes:
- A design-informed blueprint generator (already is)
- That launches coding agents with scoped briefs (already does)
- And **shows you what they built** (new)
- And **lets you iterate** (new)

That's a genuinely differentiated tool. T3 Code wraps agents for any codebase. Claude Design is closed and Anthropic-only. Open Design is agent-native but produces slop. Cauldron's edge is the design pipeline in front of the agents — the clarification, blueprinting, design system selection, quality scoring. The bidirectional integration just closes the loop on the output side.

---

## Next Steps (If Approved)

1. Billy reviews this scope and decides on tier target
2. If Tier 1: Bobbi implements process tracking + status endpoint (1-2 days)
3. If Tier 2: extend handoff prompts + add result scanner (2-3 days)
4. If Tier 3: defer to a future sprint — requires dedicated UI work
5. All changes go through the existing PR + weekly QA pipeline
6. Update this Obsidian note with the decision and any implementation notes

# Cauldron OS — Camillo UX Research

> **Product:** Cauldron OS unified (v0.240)
> **Scope:** Product identity, user journey, design language, casual/power toggle, macOS native (deferred)
> **Position:** Design lead verdict for the unification
> **Consulted:** Public `cauldron-os` repo, private `cauldron` repo, WDL brand standard

---

## 1. Product Identity

### What the unified Cauldron OS feels like

The unified Cauldron OS is not a dev-tool. It is not a SaaS dashboard. It is a **design intelligence forge** — a dark workshop where raw ideas get interrogated, refined, and cast into blueprints and working prototypes.

Think: *A master craftsperson's workshop at midnight. Tools are organised. The forge is hot. The lighting is deliberate. Everything serves the act of making something good.*

The public Cauldron OS currently reads as "competent open-source project generator." It works but has no soul. The private Cauldron reads as "Billy's personal cyber-witch factory" — distinctive but insular. The unification must land between these: **approachable enough for a hobbyist to open in a browser; deep enough for a professional to build production apps.**

| Attribute | Public v2.3 | Private v3.0 | Unified Target |
|-----------|-------------|--------------|----------------|
| Vibe | Generic dark dev-tool | Cyber-witch forge | **Dark atelier** |
| Palette | Tailwind obsidian + neon purple | Deep-950 + acid green | **Private's palette, refined** |
| Typography | System-ui + JetBrains Mono | Barlow + Barlow SC + JetBrains Mono | **Barlow SC heads, Barlow body, JetBrains Mono code** |
| Layout | 3-panel (dump → blueprint → preview) | 6-stage pipeline (dump → interrogate → system → blueprint → prototype → export) | **6-stage pipeline (winning pattern)** |
| Character | None — Tailwind default | Tons — acid green, purple glow, noise texture | **Distinctive but intentional** |

### Decision: Name

**Stick with "Cauldron OS."** It has recognition in the open-source community (the public repo has existing users, GitHub stars, workflows). A name change introduces confusion with zero offsetting benefit. The version reset to `v0.240` already signals a major change.

The private "Cauldron 3" becomes "Cauldron OS v0.240."

### One-Sentence Positioning Statement

> **Cauldron OS turns raw ideas into design-aware blueprints and working prototypes — a local-first forge for indie builders who refuse to ship ugly.**

### The Brand Aesthetic Heart

The unified product needs a single, coherent design language. I've studied all three sources of truth:

1. **Public Cauldron:** Tailwind obsidian palette (#0d0d0f bg), neon purple accent (#b794f6), system-ui fonts. Generic "dark mode SaaS" — plays it safe, has no identity.

2. **Private Cauldron:** Deep-950 (#07080d) background, layered radial gradients (acid green, pink, purple), acid green #c1ff00 primary accent, purple #8b5cf6 secondary, pink #f472b6 tertiary. Barlow font family. Noise texture overlay. Glassmorphism panels with colored borders. This is **distinctive, intentional, and memorable.**

3. **WDL Brand Standard:** Bone white (#F9F6EE) background, Playfair Display serif headlines, Space Mono labels, muted pastel cards. Retro-modern editorial. Beautiful for a marketing site. **Wrong for a developer tool.**

**Decision:** The private Cauldron's design language carries forward. It is the only one of the three that has genuine character while functioning as a tool interface. The WDL brand standard is for the *landing page* and *marketing site* — not the application itself. The unified Cauldron OS app gets the dark forge aesthetic; the witchdaddylabs.com marketing gets the editorial bone-white treatment. These are complementary, not competing.

---

## 2. User Journey Mapping

### Casual User Path

**Entry point:** Lands on the app, sees the 6-stage pipeline rail at the top with "Brain Dump" highlighted as the active stage. Single textarea with placeholder copy. No configuration visible.

**How the UI reveals next steps:**
- Stage 1 (Brain Dump): large textarea, subtle helper text. Two buttons at bottom: "Interrogate" and "Generate Blueprint." The casual user ignores Interrogate.
- Clicking "Generate Blueprint" prompts for an API key if not set. A simple API key modal appears once, then the key is saved in localStorage.
- After generation: Stage 4 (Blueprint) lights up. Stage rail shows progress.
- User sees the blueprint. Buttons: "Download Blueprint (Markdown)" and "Export JSON."
- They download and leave. Total engagement: 3-5 minutes.

**Divergence point:** The casual path diverges at Stage 1. The casual user skips "Interrogate" (Stage 2) and "Taste Engine" (Stage 3) entirely, jumping straight to blueprint generation with default settings.

**Aha moment:** "I dumped a messy paragraph about my app idea and it returned a complete, structured blueprint with architecture decisions, component hierarchy, and data flow. This actually works."

**Restrictions/mode:** In casual mode, only Stages 1, 4 (generate), and 5 (export) are visible. Stages 2 (interrogate), 3 (taste engine), and 6 (handoff) are collapsed behind a progressive disclosure affordance — a subtle "Show advanced" link.

### Power User Path

**Entry point:** Same landing — the 6-stage pipeline rail. But power-user settings persisted (model selection, stage routing, design reference prefs) from their last session rehydrate the UI.

**How the UI reveals next steps:**
- Stage 1: Brain dump as before, but the power user's model selector, provider dropdown, and settings gear are all visible.
- They write their dump, click "Interrogate" (Stage 2 lights up).
- Stage 2: AI-generated questions appear. They answer some, skip others. Click "Send to Design System."
- Stage 3 (Taste Engine): Design reference dropdown with preview thumbnails, reference URL with deep research mode toggle, scaffold template selector. They pick a reference, see a visual preview card, hit "Research URL" for deep Playwright scrape.
- Stage 4 (Blueprint): Generate. The blueprint appears in the workspace panel AND a live HTML/AlpineJS prototype renders in the preview panel simultaneously.
- Stage 5 (Prototype): They toggle between prototype view and blueprint code. Make refinement requests in a chat input.
- Stage 6 (Export / Handoff): They pick a target tool (OpenCode, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, etc.), scaffold the project, and hand it off with all context.

**Divergence point:** The power path diverges from the moment they click "Interrogate" instead of "Generate Blueprint." Every subsequent stage is the power path. The casual user never sees stages 2, 3, or 6 unless they opt in.

**Aha moment:** "I chose the Stripe design reference, fed it a URL, and it generated a complete working HTML prototype that actually looks like Stripe — then exported it as a Cursor-ready project folder with `@.cursorrules`, architecture doc, and a scaffolded Next.js project. I just saved 4 hours of setup."

### Light Mode vs Dark Mode Decision

**Decision:** Dark mode is the default. Light mode exists but is secondary.

**Rationale:**
- Both current Cauldrons are dark-mode native. Switching to light-mode default would alienate existing users and waste the design system equity built in the private repo.
- Dark mode signals "serious tool" vs "casual web app." This matters for positioning.
- The WDL brand standard (bone white) is for *marketing*, not the app.

**Toggle behavior:**
- Setting stored in localStorage, synced to `prefers-color-scheme` if no explicit preference is set.
- Toggle location: settings panel, not in the main chrome. Power users who need light mode will find it. Casual users won't care.
- Light mode transforms the palette: deep-950 → bone white, acid green → navy blue (#1A222E), glass panels become frosted white glass. The structure remains identical.

---

## 3. Design Language

### Carried Forward Design System

**Source:** Private Cauldron's `tokens.css` with modifications.

**Why not the WDL brand standard?**
The WDL brand standard (bone white, Playfair Display, pastel cards) is editorial, magazine-esque, and beautiful for a *portfolio site*. It would make Cauldron OS look like a design blog, not a tool. The private Cauldron's palette is tool-native — dark, immersive, with the acid green providing energy without being juvenile. It's a genuine design opinion, not a copy of Linear/Vercel/Raycast.

**Modifications from the private Cauldron's current tokens:**

#### Palette (Refined)

| Token | Current (Private) | Unified Recommendation | Notes |
|-------|-------------------|----------------------|-------|
| `--deep-950` | `#07080d` | `#07080d` | **Keep.** Perfect. |
| `--deep-900` | `#0a0c12` | `#0a0c12` | Keep |
| `--deep-850` | `#10131b` | `#10131b` | Keep |
| `--charcoal-900` | `#141821` | `#141821` | Keep |
| `--charcoal-850` | `#1a1f2b` | `#1f2937`suggest | Actually keep as-is |
| `--bone-50` | `#fffdf7` | `#fffdf7` | Keep — used in light mode and iframe backgrounds |
| `--bone-100` | `#f9f6ee` | `#f9f6ee` | Keep — WDL brand bridge |
| `--acid-400` | `#d8ff4f` | `#d8ff4f` | Keep |
| `--acid-500` | `#c1ff00` | `#c1ff00` | **Keep. This is the Cauldron color.** |
| `--purple-400` | `#a78bfa` | `#a78bfa` | Keep — secondary accent |
| `--purple-500` | `#8b5cf6` | `#8b5cf6` | Keep |
| `--pink-400` | `#f472b6` | `#f472b6` | Keep — tertiary accent |
| `--text-strong` | `#f8faf4` | `#f8faf4` | Keep |
| `--text` | `#e7ece2` | `#e7ece2` | Keep |
| `--text-muted` | `#a9b1a9` | `#a9b1a9` | Keep |

**No changes needed.** The palette is already correct. The unification needs to apply these tokens to the public Cauldron's components, not change the private Cauldron's palette.

#### Typography (Refined)

Current private: Barlow Semi Condensed (display), Barlow (body), JetBrains Mono (code).

**Keep this.** It works. Barlow SC gives condensed, authoritative headlines. Barlow body is clean at every weight. JetBrains Mono is the best code face for tools.

**Addition:** Introduce Space Mono from the WDL brand standard for metadata labels, timestamps, and status indicators. This bridges the brand standard into the app without disrupting the existing hierarchy.

| Role | Font | Size | Weight | Tracking |
|------|------|------|--------|----------|
| Main title | Barlow SC | 28-42px | 800 | -0.04em |
| Section heading | Barlow SC | 34-58px | 700 | -0.025em |
| Stage heading | Barlow SC | 24-34px | 700 | uppercase |
| Body | Barlow | 15-18px | 400-500 | normal |
| Code | JetBrains Mono | 13-14px | 400 | normal |
| **Labels/metadata** | **Space Mono** | **11-12px** | **700** | **0.12-0.24em** |
| Status string | Space Mono | 12px | 400 | 0.06em |

#### Key UI Patterns to Carry Forward

**From the private Cauldron (carry forward):**
1. ✅ Acid green (#c1ff00) as the primary action color
2. ✅ Purple borders on workspace panel, acid borders on preview panel
3. ✅ Glassmorphism panels with colored border differentiation
4. ✅ Noise texture overlay (low opacity)
5. ✅ Radial gradient background (acid at top-left, pink at top-right, purple at bottom)
6. ✅ The 6-stage pipeline rail with stage-tab buttons
7. ✅ The `kicker` pattern (Space Mono uppercase code-styled label above headings)
8. ✅ Status bar at bottom always showing model state
9. ✅ Toast notification stack

**From the public Cauldron (carry forward):**
1. ✅ The 3-panel layout (workspace + preview) as the inner content area
2. ✅ Design reference dropdown (expand with previews)
3. ✅ Markdown/JSON export
4. ✅ The "Interrogate" button (renamed to "Interrogate Brief")
5. ✅ GitHub community standards (not a UI concern but part of the product)

**From the WDL brand standard (selectively import):**
1. ✅ Space Mono for labels and metadata (instead of JetBrains Mono for these roles)
2. ✅ The editorial divider style (1px line, 60% width)
3. ✅ The frosted glass navigation concept (already present in private — refine it)
4. ❌ Bone white backgrounds (app stays dark)
5. ❌ Playfair Display (wrong tone for a tool)
6. ❌ Muted pastel cards (wrong palette)

### Light Mode Design

Light mode inverts the palette while keeping the structure identical:

| Dark Token | Light Equivalent |
|------------|------------------|
| `--deep-950` | `--bone-100` (#f9f6ee) |
| `--deep-900` | `--white` (#ffffff) |
| `--acid-500` | `--purple-500` (#8b5cf6) — the accent should be a saturated color in light mode, not green |
| `--text-strong` | `--navy` (#1a222e) |
| `--text` | `--navy` @ 85% |
| `--text-muted` | `--navy` @ 55% |
| Panel backgrounds | White with frosted glass |
| Border colors | `rgba(26, 34, 46, 0.10)` |

Light mode uses the WDL brand standard's navy for text — bridging the brand standard naturally.

### Toggle Experience

Settings panel, "Appearance" tab:
- "Theme: Dark / Light / System"
- System respects `prefers-color-scheme`
- Applied immediately, persisted to localStorage
- No animated transition — instantaneous swap to avoid layout thrash

---

## 4. Casual / Power Toggle

### Decision: Progressive Disclosure, Not a Toggle

**Do NOT add a "Casual / Power" toggle switch.** It's a UX crutch that:
- Forces users to self-identify before they know what the app can do
- Adds a cognitive overhead on first visit ("What am I?")
- Creates feature-discovery cliffs — things hidden behind the wrong label
- Doubles QA surface area

**Instead: Progressive disclosure through stage revelation.**

### How It Works

All users see the **6-stage pipeline rail**. However:

**First visit (no saved state):**
- Stage 1 (Brain Dump) is active. The other 5 stages are visible as greyed-out tab buttons with lock icons.
- Hovering over a locked stage shows a tooltip: "Complete the previous stage first."
- Below the brain dump textarea: two action buttons — "Interrogate Brief" and "Generate Blueprint."

**The branching logic:**
- If user clicks **"Generate Blueprint"** directly: The app auto-selects a default design reference ("None"), skips interrogation, generates the blueprint. Stages 2-3 remain collapsed. Stage 4 lights up. Stage 5 (export) becomes available after generation. Stage 6 (handoff) remains locked.
  - *This is the casual path.* The user never sees interrogate, taste engine, or handoff.
- If user clicks **"Interrogate Brief"** first: Stage 2 unlocks dynamically (tab becomes clickable, no lock). The pipeline visually shifts to show the full depth.
  - *This is the power path reveal.* Once they engage with interrogation, all stages unlock progressively.

**What this means for the UI:**
- No toggle. No settings switch. No mode selector.
- The pipeline rail itself is the navigation and the mode-reveal mechanism.
- Power features are not *hidden* — they're *deferred*. The user sees the full path (6 stages) but can only walk forward one step at a time.
- The branch point is a single binary action: "Skip interrogation" vs "Engage interrogation."

### What Each Mode Shows

| Component | Casual (skip interrogate) | Power (engage interrogate) |
|-----------|--------------------------|---------------------------|
| Stage 1 — Brain Dump | Full UI | Full UI |
| Stage 2 — Interrogate | Locked (greyed) | Unlocked, answer questions |
| Stage 3 — Taste Engine | Locked (auto defaults) | Full (design ref + research + template) |
| Stage 4 — Blueprint | Generate with defaults | Generate with all context |
| Stage 5 — Prototype | View + download | View + refine via chat |
| Stage 6 — Export | Download Markdown/JSON | Handoff menu (10+ tools) |
| Settings gear | Minimal (API key) | Full (stage routing, models, themes) |

### Migration Path

For existing users of the public Cauldron who have saved state (model selections, API keys, design refs), the progressive disclosure retains their settings. The pipeline auto-unlocks stages they've used before (if they had a saved draft with interrogation data, stage 2 is pre-unlocked).

---

## 5. macOS Native (Deferred)

### Confirmation

**Not pursuing macOS native for v1.** The unified product ships as a browser-based application. Rationale:
- The public Cauldron OS is already browser-native with ~51 files and an Express backend
- A native shell adds build complexity, distribution signing, and maintenance overhead
- No user demand signal exists yet (zero requests in the public repo's issue tracker)
- The product needs to prove product-market fit first

### Future Path: Tauri v2

Tauri v2 is the correct path when the time comes:
- Frontend is already HTML + AlpineJS — zero rewrite needed
- Rust shell provides native filesystem access, system notifications, menu bar, and window management
- Bundle size: ~5MB vs 150MB+ for Electron
- macOS entitlements via `entitlements.plist` for sandboxed file access

### macOS-Native Features Tauri Could Unlock

| Feature | macOS Mechanism | UX Value |
|---------|----------------|----------|
| **Filesystem hooks** | FSEvents / kqueue | Watch project folders for changes; auto-refresh build status |
| **Dock integration** | NSApplication | Badge unread drafts count, provide "New Blueprint" contextual menu |
| **Notification Center** | UserNotifications | Long-running build complete, research done — works even when app is backgrounded |
| **Spotlight indexing** | Core Spotlight | Index generated blueprints, allow macOS search to find them |
| **System tray** | NSStatusBar | Quick-action menu: paste URL from clipboard, new draft, recent projects |
| **Drag-and-drop** | NSDragOperation | Drop a URL from Safari directly into the brain dump; drop a folder to import |
| **Touch Bar** | NSTouchBar | (Diminishing value — modern MacBooks don't have it) |
| **Menu bar** | NSMenu | Proper macOS app menu with Command-period, standard shortcuts, services menu |
| **Window management** | NSWindow | Native titlebar, tab groups, full-screen support, window restoration |

### When to Revisit: Watch Signals

**Revisit the native app decision when any of these signals hit:**

| Signal | Threshold | Priority |
|--------|-----------|----------|
| GitHub stars + forks | >500 stars, >50 forks | Medium |
| Weekly active users (telemetry) | >200 weekly sessions | High |
| Feature requests for desktop features | 5+ distinct GitHub issues asking for desktop app | High |
| User complaints about browser limitations | "Can't save files to a custom location" / "Browser storage limits" | Medium |
| Funding / sponsorship | >=$500/month in GitHub Sponsors or equivalent | High |
| Tauri v2 reaches stable 2.0 | Currently in release candidate | Low (prep work can start) |
| Another developer tool successfully ships Tauri v2 app | First-mover case study proves the path | Low |
| Cauldron OS is used for >10 production deploys | Community dependency signal | Medium |

**Recommended cadence for re-evaluation:** Every 3 months, check these signals. If 3+ signals are green simultaneously → start Tauri v2 prototyping.

---

## 6. Camillo's Recommendation

### Product Identity

**Name:** Cauldron OS (unchanged)
**Version:** v0.240 (as per Billy's proposal)
**One-liner:** *Raw ideas → forged blueprints + working prototypes. A local-first design forge for indie builders who refuse to ship ugly.*
**Tagline for header:** "Brain dump → interrogation → taste engine → blueprint → prototype → handoff."

### Design Language Direction

**Primary identity:** Private Cauldron's dark forge aesthetic. This is the unified Cauldron OS's DNA.

**Design system carried forward:** The private Cauldron's tokens.css with zero palette changes, plus:
- Add Space Mono (from WDL brand standard) for metadata labels
- Keep Barlow SC + Barlow + JetBrains Mono as the core font stack
- Light mode inverts the palette using WDL navy #1A222E as text, bone white #F9F6EE as bg

**Colour swatches (dark mode primary):**

```
Background        ██ #07080d  (deep-950)
Panels            ██ #141821  (charcoal-900) 
Primary accent    ██ #c1ff00  (acid-500)
Secondary accent  ██ #8b5cf6  (purple-500)
Tertiary accent   ██ #f472b6  (pink-400)
Text strong       ██ #f8faf4
Text body         ██ #e7ece2
Text muted        ██ #a9b1a9
Bone (for iframes)██ #f9f6ee  (bone-100)
```

### UX Pattern for Casual/Power

**Progressive disclosure via the 6-stage pipeline rail.**

No toggle switch. No mode selector. Users reveal power features by engaging with them:
1. All users land on the same screen with the same 6-stage rail.
2. "Interrogate Brief" is the branching point — skip it for casual, engage it for power.
3. Locked stages are visible (deferred, not hidden) with clear progression cues.
4. Settings panel reveals more controls as the user accumulates history and saved state.

This is simpler to build, simpler to test, and respects the user's intelligence.

### Top 3 Features the Unified Product Should NOT Ship Without

1. **The 6-stage pipeline UI** (private's frontend architecture). This is the UX container that makes everything else cohere. Without it, the unified product is just the public Cauldron with more API routes bolted on. The pipeline gives the product its identity as a *process*, not a form.

2. **The visual design language** (private's tokens.css + app.css). The unified product MUST carry forward the acid green, the radial gradients, the glass panels, the noise texture, the colored border differentiation between workspace (purple) and preview (acid). This is the single biggest differentiator from every other "AI code generator."

3. **Multi-tool handoff** (Billy's Proposal 2, expanded). The unified Cauldron generates blueprints and prototypes. But the *value* is in handing that work off to the right builder tool. Without multi-tool handoff, users hit a wall at export — "great, now I have a markdown file, what do I do with it?" Handoff to OpenCode, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Aider, and the rest makes the product a bridge, not a dead end.

### What I'd Personally Want in the v3.0 Landing Page

The landing page (witchdaddylabs.com/cauldron) uses the **WDL brand standard** (bone white, Playfair Display, editorial layout). This is the marketing face. The *app* is the dark forge. The *landing page* is the invitation.

I want:

1. **Hero section:** Split layout. Left side: bone white editorial card with the one-liner and a single CTA: "Open Cauldron OS →" (styled as a dark pill button against the bone white background). Right side: a live, looped screen recording of the unified Cauldron — a brain dump being typed, then the pipeline stages lighting up in sequence, ending with a preview rendering. The recording window has a subtle acid green glow border.

2. **Pipeline visual:** Beneath the hero, an animated horizontal version of the 6-stage pipeline — each stage is a bone white card with the stage icon and label. When you scroll past, each stage lights up sequentially with acid green or purple. The copy for each stage is a single line: "Dump your idea messily." / "Answer what matters." / "Choose your design DNA." / "Generate the spec + prototype." / "Preview. Refine. Iterate." / "Hand off to your builder of choice."

3. **"Works with" section:** A grid of builder tool logos (OpenCode, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Aider, Continue, Copilot CLI, Codex CLI) arranged as a marquee or card grid. Each shows a brief "how it works" hover state. This signals *ecosystem*, not lock-in.

4. **"Before / After" comparison:** Two columns. Left: "Raw brain dump" — a messy textarea with placeholder brain dump text. Right: "Blueprint + prototype" — a rendered preview of the generated HTML. Arrow between them saying "Cauldron OS processes this in ~30 seconds."

5. **Design language showcase:** A muted pastel card with a subtle "Cauldron OS design tokens" label — showing the three accent colors (acid green, purple, pink) as small painted swatches. This signals to design-aware visitors that the product has taste.

6. **The toggle in marketing only:** On the landing page only, a subtle "Dark mode / Light mode" toggle in the page's top nav that switches the landing page itself between bone-white editorial (default) and dark forge (for atmosphere). This demonstrates the product's duality without cluttering the app.

7. **Footer:** "Built by Witch Daddy Labs" in Space Mono. No newsletter signup. No "Subscribe for updates." Just "Built by Witch Daddy Labs · MIT licensed · v0.240" — the landing page should be as clean as the app should be deep.

---

## Summary Decision Matrix

| Question | Decision | Rationale |
|----------|----------|-----------|
| Name | Cauldron OS (unchanged) | Existing recognition, v0.240 signals freshness |
| Design direction | Private Cauldron's dark forge | Distinctive, functional, already works |
| Design system source | Private `tokens.css` + Space Mono from WDL brand | Best of both worlds |
| Dark vs light mode | Dark primary, light secondary, toggle in Settings | Dark is tool-native; light for accessibility |
| Casual/power pattern | Progressive disclosure via pipeline rail | No toggle crutch; users self-select by action |
| 6-stage pipeline | Carry forward from private | The winning UX pattern |
| macOS native v1 | Deferred | Browser-based until demand signal hits |
| Tauri path | When: 3+ watch signals green | Rust-native shell, zero frontend rewrite |
| Light mode palette | Inverted: bone white bg, navy text | Bridges WDL brand standard naturally |
| Font stack | Barlow SC (heads) + Barlow (body) + JetBrains Mono (code) + Space Mono (labels) | Proven in private; Space Mono adds brand bridge |
| Landing page style | WDL brand standard (bone white, editorial) | Marketing ≠ app; complementary, not competing |

# Cauldron OS — Unification Plan

> *Created 2026-05-16 by Claudia — based on Claude-driven repo exploration*
> **Public repo:** `cre8tivoz/cauldron-os` (unified)
> **Current version:** v0.250.0
> **Plan status:** ✅ Complete — 4 sprints delivered

**NOTE FROM BILLY — 16th May:**
> Axial workflow is proven. Use it as a baseline for Cauldron unification. We should merge the best of the private build into public Cauldron OS so they are one product. Camillo should do thorough UX research on what the unified product should look and feel like. macOS native app is an option we note but don't pursue now.

---
**GITHUB TOKEN FOR HERMES — stored in ~/.hermes/.env — 30 days from 16 May**

## Overview

**What this is:** A plan to merge two codebases — the **public Cauldron OS** (open-source blueprint generator on GitHub) and the **private Cauldron** (Billy's local Witch Daddy Labs product factory) — into a **single, unified product**.

**Why now:** The public/private split was a necessary first step to open-source the blueprint generator safely. But the private build has accumulated features the public needs (XML tool agent, build mode, deep research, template system, project management). The public build has community standards the private needs (CI/CD, issue templates, licensing). Unifying them makes one stronger product instead of maintaining two diverging forks.

**Product philosophy:** "Brain dump → design-aware blueprint → HTML preview → scaffold → build → export." The public Cauldron stops at blueprint. The private Cauldron goes all the way to build execution. The unified product should offer the full pipeline — but with a toggle so casual users stop at blueprint while power users go all the way to build.

**Licensing:** Public is MIT. Private is ISC (unpublished). After unification, the unified product stays MIT-licensed for the open-source core. Private WDL workflows (project records, Obsidian hooks, agent orchestration) stay local-only, excluded from the open build but present when you self-host.

---

## Current State — Both Repos

### Unified Cauldron OS (`cauldron-os`)

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Version** | v0.250.0 (pre-1.0 semver) |
| **Stack** | Node.js, Express 5.x, sql.js (SQLite), AlpineJS, Playwright |
| **Database** | 4 tables: drafts, sessions, research_history, project_status_overrides |
| **Key features** | 7-stage pipeline (dump → interrogate → system → blueprint → prototype → build → export), XML Tool Agent System (7 tools, multi-turn), sandboxed build workspace with file listing + live preview, Deep Playwright research (screenshots + CSS extraction), 4 scaffold templates, 27 design references (13 brands + 14 Refero), URL research sweep, Annoying PM mode, draft/history management, OpenCode handoff, project import, stage model routing |
| **Cloud models** | OpenAI-compatible (any), Google Gemini, Ollama local |
| **Frontend** | AlpineJS SPA with custom dark forge tokens |
| **Community** | GitHub workflows, issue/PR templates, Code of Conduct, MIT license |
| **Platform** | GitHub: `cre8tivoz/cauldron-os` |

### Private Cauldron (`/Users/habibi/hermes/cre8tivoz/cauldron`)
> **Archived** — features ported to unified codebase in Sprints 1–3. Retained locally for WDL-specific project records and agent configurations that stay private.

---

## Key Differences — What Goes Where

### 🟢 Goes Public (safe to open-source)

| Feature | Source | Why it's safe |
|---------|--------|--------------|
| XML Tool Agent System | private `lib/` | Generic build agent — no WDL-specific data |
| Build mode (real file writes) | private `/api/build/*` | Sandboxed per-session — no host access |
| 4 scaffold templates | private `/api/templates` | Generic project templates |
| Deep Playwright research | private `scrapeRenderedURL()` | Browser automation — no private data |
| 14 Refero design styles | private | Public DESIGN.md references |
| Research history table | private `research_history` | Research data, not project secrets |
| Stage model routing | private | Just config — no keys in code |
| Build status dashboard | private `/api/build-status` | Project folder scanning — generic |
| Project import | private `/api/projects/import` | Reconstructs from README/package — generic |
| 6-stage pipeline frontend | private `public/` | The UI itself, not the data behind it |
| Cloud provider routing | private | Just API call orchestration |
| Chat proxy endpoint | private `/api/chat/completions` | Generic OpenAI-compatible proxy |

### 🔴 Stays Private (local-only)

| Feature | Reason |
|---------|--------|
| WDL project records in `projects/` | Contains Billy's product ideas, build history, decisions |
| Obsidian-specific automations | Personal workflow, not generalisable |
| Project status overrides with Billy's notes | Decision-state tracking — personal |
| Minion agent integrations | Billy's private agent team setup |
| Home Assistant / n8n / webhook experiments | Personal infrastructure |
| Autonomous build/test loops | WDL-specific CI patterns |
| Private research memory tied to projects | Associated with WDL product decisions |
| MemPalace configs + indexed data | Linked to Billy's vault, not generalisable |

### 🟡 Optional — Could Go Either Way

| Feature | Decision | Reasoning |
|---------|----------|-----------|
| Master Brain taste layer | **Goes public** | The anti-pattern guide and design taste injection is the secret sauce. Making it public builds trust. Keep it as an opt-in feature. |
| OpenCode launch actions | **Goes public** | Generic — launches a terminal with a prompt. Users of any IDE could benefit. |
| OpenCode handoff (stubs) | **Goes public** | Already half-public (stubs in public repo). Formalise. |

---

## Camillo UX Research Scope

Camillo should research and report on the following before any code merging begins:

### 1. Product Identity
- What does one unified Cauldron OS *feel* like?
- Current public Cauldron: functional, technical, dev-tool vibes (Tailwind CDN, vanilla JS)
- Current private Cauldron: dark SaaS, cyber-witch aesthetic (custom tokens, stage pipeline)
- **Question:** Do we keep the dark witch aesthetic or evolve into something more accessible?
- **Question:** Does the unified product need a new name or just "Cauldron OS v3"?

### 2. User Journey Mapping
- **Casual user path:** Open the app → Brain Dump → pick design reference → generate blueprint → export Markdown → done
- **Power user path:** Open → Brain Dump → interrogate → design → generate → scaffold real project → build in workspace → deploy
- **Question:** How do we design the UI so the casual path is obvious but the power path is discoverable?
- **Question:** Should the casual path default to a light, approachable UI and the power path reveal the dark mode?
- **Question:** How do we onboard users without overwhelming them?

### 3. Design Language
- Current public: plays it safe (Tailwind defaults, standard form layouts)
- Current private: distinctive (dark palette, acid green accent, stage pipeline with progress indicators)
- **Question:** What design system do we carry forward? The WDL brand standard (bone white, Playfair, Space Mono) or the Cauldron 3 app palette (deep charcoals, acid green)?
- **Question:** Could the unified product have both — light mode for casual browsing, dark mode for deep work?

### 4. Feature Prioritisation
- Which private features matter most to ship first in the unified product?
- Order candidates:
  1. XML Tool Agent System (biggest differentiator)
  2. Deep Playwright research (biggest UX upgrade)
  3. 4 scaffold templates (biggest productivity boost)
  4. 6-stage pipeline UI (biggest visual upgrade)
  5. Research history + favorites
  6. Build status dashboard

### 5. macOS Native App — Deferred
- **Research question:** Is a macOS native app (SwiftUI, Electron, or Tauri) a viable future direction?
- **Decision:** Not now. Stay browser-based for v1 of the unified product.
- **Rationale:** The public is already browser-based. A native app adds build complexity, distribution friction, and a maintenance burden that's not justified until the product has proven adoption.
- **Note:** If adoption grows, Tauri is the most natural path — write the frontend once (HTML/JS/AlpineJS) and wrap it in a Rust native shell with filesystem hooks. macOS entitlements for file access, notifications, and deep links would unlock the "downloadable desktop app" positioning.
- **Keep watching:** Tauri v2 stability, Electron's resource usage improvements, and whether users ask for a desktop experience.

## Refinement Workflow

## Billy's Proposals — Incorporated

### Proposal 1: Codebase Location
**Decision:** The unified codebase lives at `/Users/habibi/hermes/app-codebases/cauldron-os/` alongside other app codebases.

**Why:** Keeps Cauldron OS in the same neighbourhood as AXIAL APP and other built products rather than buried inside the witch-daddy-labs design folder. Signals that it's a real app, not just a design experiment.

**Action in Sprint 1:** Create directory, clone/copy merged repo, verify paths resolve, update any hardcoded references in launcher scripts and documentation.

---

### Proposal 2: Multi-Tool Handoff
**Decision:** Replace the current OpenCode-only handoff stub with a **handoff menu** supporting multiple target tools.

**Target tools to support:**

| Tool | Type | Notes |
|------|------|-------|
| OpenCode | CLI | Already implemented (stubs exist). Full implementation |
| Claude Code | CLI (ACP) | `claude --acp --stdio` — growing fast |
| Codex CLI | CLI | OpenAI's coding agent, rising adoption |
| Cursor | IDE | Most popular AI IDE. Export as `.cursorrules` + project folder |
| Windsurf | IDE | Growing fast in dev tool space. Export as `.windsurfrules` |
| Aider | CLI | Popular open-source CLI coding assistant. Export prompt file |
| Continue.dev | IDE Plugin | Open-source AI coding plugin. Export as `.continuerc.json` |
| Hermes Agent | CLI/Agent | "Hermes agent persona" style handoff. Export as SKILL.md + brief |
| OpenClaw | CLI/Agent | Agentic coding tool. Export in OpenClaw-compatible format |
| GitHub Copilot CLI | CLI | `github-copilot-cli` — export as `.github/copilot-instructions.md` |

**Implementation approach:**
- Each target gets a **handoff template** (markdown file, config snippet, or folder scaffolding)
- The UI presents a clean target selector after blueprint generation
- Selected tool receives: project description, architecture summary, key constraints, tech stack, generated blueprint
- Default selection: "Download blueprint + prototype" (no-commitment option that always works)

**Why this matters:** A blueprint generator that only hands off to one tool limits its audience. Different developers use different tools — supporting the ecosystem makes Cauldron OS useful to more people without us having to guess which tool wins.

---

### Proposal 3: Versioning Reset
**Decision:** Reset versioning on unification. The product never shipped a true 1.0 — calling it v2.x was aspirational. Going to `0.240` sets honest pre-1.0 semver: Cauldron OS is actively evolving toward a stable release.

**Implementation:**

Instead of hunting through git history to retroactively fix every old CHANGELOG entry, docs reference, and MANIFEST mention, we do a **clean break at unification**:

1. `package.json` version → `0.240.0`
2. `README.md` banner → `v0.240`
3. `CHANGELOG.md` — starts fresh with a new entry: "0.240.0 — Unification Sprint 1 · 2026-05-16"
4. `server.js` startup banner → `Cauldron OS v0.240`
5. `MANIFEST.md`, `GETTING_STARTED.md`, `FUNDING.yml` updated as touched during sprints
6. Old CHANGELOG archived under `docs/history/CHANGELOG-2.x.md`

**Rationale:** A clean break avoids fragile retroactive git history edits. Future readers see "0.240+" in the current docs and can find the pre-unification history in the archive if needed. The note at the top of the new CHANGELOG reads: *"Cauldron OS was versioned 2.0–2.4 in its public repo. Starting from Sprint 1, versions use pre-1.0 semver (0.240+) to reflect that this is an actively evolving pre-stable product."*

This is pragmatic, honest, and doesn't waste effort on cosmetic history rewriting.

# Cauldron OS — v0.40 Release Plan

> **Author:** Claudia (COO, Witch Daddy Labs)
> **Date:** 2026-06-03
> **Status:** Draft — ready for Codex execution

---

## Goal

Take Cauldron OS from a solid v0.30 (design-to-prototype pipeline) to v0.40 — a more useful, more shareable, more "holy shit this is clever" tool. Focus on features that make people want to fork it.

---

## Phase 0: Delegation Setup

**Owner:** Claudia (orchestration) + Codex (implementation)

1. Create `docs/RELEASE_PLAN_v0.40.md` (this file)
2. Ensure AGENTS.md is up to date with current architecture
3. Define public interfaces for new subsystems

---

## Phase 1: Blueprint Diffing

**Owner:** Codex

**Problem:** When you iterate on a blueprint, you can't see what changed between versions.

**Solution:**
- After each blueprint generation/refinement, diff against the previous version
- Show a unified diff view in the panel (additions in green, deletions in red)
- Store blueprint versions in the draft record
- Add a "Version history" dropdown to the blueprint panel: v1, v2, v3...

**Files:**
- `routes/generation.js` — add diff endpoint
- `public/scripts/app.js` — diff display logic
- `public/index.html` — version history UI
- `db/index.js` — blueprint version storage

**Effort:** 4-6 hours

---

## Phase 2: Multi-Agent Build Orchestration

**Owner:** Codex

**Problem:** The build stage hands off to one agent. Real projects need multiple agents (e.g., Cursor for frontend, Codex for tests).

**Solution:**
- In the Build stage, allow selecting multiple agents
- Generate separate handoff packages per agent with scoped prompts
- Example: "Cursor gets the UI components, Codex gets the API routes, Claude Code gets the tests"
- Show per-agent build status in the pipeline log

**Files:**
- `routes/build-agents.js` — multi-agent orchestration
- `lib/handoff-package.js` — scoped prompt generation
- `public/scripts/app.js` — multi-agent UI
- `public/index.html` — agent selection checkboxes

**Effort:** 6-8 hours

---

## Phase 3: Plugin/Scaffold Marketplace (Community)

**Owner:** Codex

**Problem:** People can't easily share their DESIGN.md systems or scaffold templates.

**Solution:**
- Add a "Community" tab to the Design Reference panel
- Establish a dedicated community GitHub repo for curated DESIGN.md files, then fetch them from that canonical source. (No `cauldron-community` repo currently exists under `cre8tivoz`.)
- Allow one-click import of community design systems
- Allow users to submit their own via PR to the community repo
- Same for scaffold templates — community Astro/Next.js starters

**Files:**
- `routes/community.js` — community content API
- `lib/design-system-catalog.js` — remote import support
- `public/scripts/app.js` — community tab UI
- `public/index.html` — community panel

**Effort:** 6-8 hours

---

## Phase 4: Build Output Quality Scoring

**Owner:** Claudia (prompt design) + Codex (implementation)

**Problem:** Cauldron generates prototypes but doesn't critique its own output before showing it to you.

**Solution:**
- After prototype generation, run a self-critique pass
- Score the prototype on: accessibility, visual hierarchy, spacing, color contrast, semantic HTML
- Show a "Quality Score" badge (A/B/C/D) next to the prototype
- If score is C or below, show specific suggestions before the user even critiques
- This is the "Annoying PM Mode for prototypes"

**Files:**
- `routes/generation.js` — quality scoring endpoint
- `lib/quality-scorer.js` — scoring logic (heuristic + LLM)
- `public/scripts/app.js` — score display
- `public/index.html` — score badge UI

**Effort:** 8-10 hours

---

## Phase 5: Polish & Release

**Owner:** Claudia (QA) + Codex (fixes)

1. Update README with v0.40 features
2. Update CHANGELOG
3. Capture new screenshots
4. Record walkthrough GIF
5. Version bump to 0.40.0
6. Tag and push
7. Write release notes for GitHub

**Effort:** 3-4 hours

---

## Delegation Map

| Phase | Work Package | Who | Method |
|-------|-------------|-----|--------|
| P0 | Setup + AGENTS.md | Claudia | Write directly |
| P1 | Blueprint diffing | Codex | Terminal + file tools |
| P2 | Multi-agent orchestration | Codex | Terminal + file tools |
| P3 | Community marketplace | Codex | Terminal + file tools |
| P4 | Quality scoring | Claudia (prompts) + Codex (impl) | Split |
| P5 | QA + release | Claudia | Direct |

---

## Risk Register

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|--------|------------|
| Multi-agent orchestration is too complex for v0.40 | Medium | High | Scope to 2-agent max (frontend + tests). Expand later. |
| Community content API depends on external repo | Medium | Medium | Start with hardcoded list. Fetch from GitHub later. |
| Quality scoring is subjective | High | Low | Use simple heuristics first (contrast ratio, semantic HTML checks). LLM scoring as enhancement. |
| Diff view breaks existing blueprint panel | Medium | Medium | Add as new tab, don't replace existing view. |

---

## Success Criteria

Cauldron OS v0.40 ships when:

- [ ] Blueprint diffing works — see what changed between versions
- [ ] Multi-agent build orchestration works — select 2+ agents, get scoped handoffs
- [ ] Community tab shows importable design systems and scaffolds
- [ ] Quality score badge appears on prototypes with specific suggestions
- [ ] All existing tests pass + new tests for diff, multi-agent, quality scoring
- [ ] README updated with v0.40 features
- [ ] Version bumped to 0.40.0

---

## Out of Scope for v0.40

- Mobile PWA (v0.50+)
- Collaborative/multi-user brewing (v0.50+)
- Desktop app (Electron/Tauri) — web-first forever
- Plugin runtime (actual code execution) — security nightmare, not worth it

# Cauldron OS Agent Guide

This guide is the first read for agents working on Cauldron OS. It keeps parallel work scoped, names the public surfaces, and points each contributor at the smallest safe edit area.

## Product Shape

Cauldron OS is a local-first, design-aware project pipeline. A user writes a rough idea, optionally runs Annoying PM Mode, selects a design reference, generates an editable blueprint, generates an HTML/AlpineJS prototype, then exports or hands the project to a build agent.

Current runtime:

- Backend: Node.js, Express 5, route modules under `routes/`.
- Frontend: static AlpineJS app in `public/index.html` and `public/scripts/app.js`.
- Styles: token-first CSS in `public/styles/tokens.css` and `public/styles/app.css`.
- Storage: local `sql.js` database through `db/index.js`.
- Agent build support: XML action loop in `lib/agent-loop.js`, workspace sandbox in `lib/workspace.js`, and project handoff routes.

## Start Here

```bash
npm install
npm start
# open http://localhost:3000
```

Validation:

```bash
npm test
```

The test suite is smoke-test oriented. Add focused smoke coverage when a change touches a route, frontend contract, generated file format, or export behavior.

## Repository Map

| Path                      | Purpose                                                                 | Safe Owners                                                        |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `server.js`               | constants, prompt helpers, route registration, shared dependency object | architecture owner only unless a task explicitly touches constants |
| `routes/generation.js`    | research, clarify, blueprint/prototype generation, `/api/handoff`       | generation/backend agent                                           |
| `routes/build.js`         | build workspace start/generate/refine/stop/files/status                 | build-agent/backend agent                                          |
| `routes/projects.js`      | project status, import, visible OpenCode resume/open flows              | handoff/backend agent                                              |
| `routes/models-design.js` | cloud/Ollama model lists, design-system API, Refero search              | design-system agent                                                |
| `routes/templates.js`     | templates and build-status API                                          | scaffold/backend agent                                             |
| `public/scripts/app.js`   | Alpine state machine, API calls, localStorage config, pipeline behavior | frontend agent                                                     |
| `public/index.html`       | app shell, stage cards, modals, preview panel                           | frontend agent                                                     |
| `public/styles/`          | visual system and responsive layout                                     | frontend/design agent                                              |
| `db/index.js`             | draft/session/research/project status schema and persistence            | data agent                                                         |
| `lib/`                    | pure utilities and XML tool agent loop                                  | build-agent/backend agent                                          |
| `docs/`                   | architecture, execution plans, public contracts                         | any agent, with care for current version language                  |
| `tests/`                  | smoke tests for public contracts                                        | owner of related feature                                           |

## Working Rules

- Branch from `main` for each PR-sized phase or work package.
- Keep PRs narrow. Do not combine unrelated v0.30 phases in one branch.
- Preserve user changes. If a file has unrelated edits, inspect before touching it and stage only intended paths.
- Prefer existing route and frontend patterns over new frameworks. The app intentionally has no frontend bundler.
- Use structured parsing or explicit schemas for generated artifacts. Avoid brittle text scraping when JSON manifests can do the job.
- Keep generated project directories under `projects/`; runtime data belongs under `data/`. Both are local runtime surfaces, not source.
- Do not print API keys or credential-bearing remote URLs in docs, tests, or logs.
- UI work should use existing CSS variables and avoid broad palette resets.
- Treat current handoff copy carefully: package creation and CLI launch are different states.

## Public Interface Boundaries

Before editing a subsystem, read `docs/PUBLIC_INTERFACES.md`. It captures the API routes, generated files, and frontend state names that other work packages depend on.

When changing an interface:

1. Update the route or manifest contract.
2. Update `docs/PUBLIC_INTERFACES.md`.
3. Add or update the relevant smoke test.
4. Mention the contract change in the PR body.

## Delegation Map For v0.30

- Phase 0: documentation, repo rules, interface contracts.
- Phase 1: design-system catalog import and validation.
- Phase 2: BYOK/CLI build-agent handoff.
- Phase 3: prototype critique and iteration history.
- Phase 4: UI polish, progress, empty states, shortcuts, settings health.
- Phase 5: real scaffold export for static HTML, Alpine, Next.js, and Astro.

Suggested parallel split:

- Backend handoff/build agent: `routes/build.js`, `routes/generation.js`, `routes/projects.js`, `lib/`.
- Frontend pipeline agent: `public/index.html`, `public/scripts/app.js`, `public/styles/`.
- Design-system agent: `server.js` design constants, `routes/models-design.js`, `design-systems/`, import/validation scripts.
- Data agent: `db/index.js`, draft/session/iteration history tests.
- Scaffold agent: `routes/templates.js`, project generation helpers, scaffold smoke tests.

## Commit And PR Expectations

- Branch names: `codex/<phase-or-feature>`.
- Commit messages: terse imperative summary.
- PRs should include changed surfaces, validation run, and any follow-up risks.
- Open draft PRs unless the user asks for ready-for-review.

## Known v0.30 Coordination Risks

- `/api/handoff` is implemented in `routes/generation.js`, while project resume/open helpers are in `routes/projects.js`.
- The current handoff route writes an OpenCode config but does not launch OpenCode.
- The Build workspace SSE routes should be verified before Phase 2 depends on them.
- `form.designReference` may contain a canonical design-system id or a Refero style/site value.
- Stage-model routing is per stage, but API-key storage is still keyed by the global provider selector.
